items.name: AMU Research Data Repository
items.description: The AMUReD Institutional Research Data Repository of the Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznan (UAM) collects and provides access to digital versions of research data collected, processed or produced as part of the scientific research or developmental work of UAM employees.

items.name: CORA.Repositori de Dades de Recerca
items.description: The CORA.Repositori de dades de Recerca (RDR) is a repository of open, curated and FAIR data that covers all academic disciplines. CORA.Repositori de dades de Recerca (RDR) is a shared service provided by participating Catalan institutions (Universities and CERCA Research Centers). The repository is managed by the CSUC and technical infrastructure is based on Dataverse.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: SearchWorks Catalog
items.description: SearchWorks is the online library catalog and discovery platform of Stanford University Libraries. It allows users to search and access millions of library resources, including books, journals, articles, digital collections, archival materials, media, and other scholarly resources held by Stanford. The platform integrates records from Stanford’s library collections and provides a single interface for discovering both physical and digital resources.

items.name: 4TU.ResearchData
items.description: 4TU.ResearchData is an international data repository for science, engineering and design, open to anyone in the world to upload and download data. Its services include curation, sharing, long-term access and preservation of research datasets. These services are available to anyone around the world. In addition, 4TU.ResearchData also offers training and resources to researchers to support them in making research data findable, accessible, interoperable and reproducible (FAIR).
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Academic Torrents
items.description: The Academic Torrents is a community-maintained distributed repository that enables researchers to share and distribute large scientific datasets and research materials using BitTorrent technology. It provides a scalable, decentralized infrastructure for hosting and downloading datasets, reducing bandwidth costs while improving data availability and reproducibility. The platform supports datasets from a wide range of scientific disciplines and allows researchers to upload, discover, and reuse openly shared research data.

items.name: ACU Research Bank
items.description: ACU Research Bank is the institutional repository of Australian Catholic University (ACU), designed to collect, preserve, and showcase the university’s research outputs. It provides access to scholarly publications, research datasets, theses, conference papers, reports, and other academic materials produced by ACU researchers and higher degree students. The repository supports open access by making research outputs discoverable and available to the global research community.

items.name: Adattár
items.description: Adattár stores research data associated with the University of Debrecen, and provides services such as data transfer, storage and sharing. As a result, research data is easily accessible and more visible to the scientific community in each field, following disciplinary standards. Adattár aims to foster best practices of findability and accessibility of research data, and will provide guidance regarding issues of access, privacy, and copyright. Adattár aims to be a widely used, inter-disciplinary, trusted platform for managing, sharing, and archiving research data created by the researchers associated with the university.

items.name: Addis Ababa University Institutional Repository
items.description: Addis Ababa University Institutional repository is an open access repository that collects, preserves, and disseminates scholarly outputs of the university.

items.name: ALADDIN
items.description: The ALADDIN database (A Labelled Atomic Data INterface) is a numerical scientific database maintained by the International Atomic Energy Agency that provides evaluated atomic, molecular, and plasma–material interaction data of interest to nuclear fusion and plasma research. It includes recommended cross sections, rate coefficients, and surface interaction data compiled from IAEA publications and coordinated research projects, supporting modelling and diagnostics of fusion plasmas and related physical processes.
subjects: Atomic, Molecular, Optical and Plasma Physics

items.name: Alberta Open Government Portal
items.description: The portal is a collection of Alberta government datasets, publications and other information products available to the public. This data and information can be used to learn about how the Alberta government works, carry out research or build web apps. The portal functions as both a library for current publications and as an archive for historic publications.

items.name: American Mineralogist Crystal Structure Database
items.description: This crystal structure database includes every structure published in the American Mineralogist, The Canadian Mineralogist, European Journal of Mineralogy and Physics and Chemistry of Minerals, as well as selected datasets from other journals.

items.name: AMS Acta
items.description: AMS Acta is the institutional open access repository which enables the researchers of the Alma Mater Studiorum - University of Bologna to share, preserve and showcase their scientific works making them easily accessible, citable and reusable. The repository collects and disseminates unpublished research such as preprints, technical reports, working papers, conference proceedings, research data and software. Moreover, it collects series and books published by the University Departments and Research teams.

items.name: Analysis and Policy Observatory
items.description: Australian Policy Online (APO) is an pen-access database and digital repository that collects, indexes, and makes public policy research and grey literature easy to find and use. It focuses mainly on policy content from Australia and New Zealand, including reports, articles, and analysis from universities, governments, think tanks, and other organisations.

items.name: Angewandte Repository
items.description: Phaidra is the digital repository of the University of Vienna in Austria. It’s an institutional platform for the long-term archiving, indexing, and secure storage of digital assets such as research data, publications, teaching materials, and multimedia.

items.name: Apollo - University of Cambridge Repository
items.description: Apollo is the institutional repository of the University of Cambridge, managed by the Open Research Systems team based in Cambridge University Library. The Repository is committed to store and preserve the University’s research outputs. Research outputs can include, but are not limited to, publications, conference proceedings, book chapters, monographs, theses, various forms of research data (video recordings, spreadsheets, computational scripts, code, images etc.), presentations and others.
licences: Apollo - University of Cambridge Repository Terms of Use

items.name: Arch
items.description: Arch is an open access repository for the research and scholarly output of Northwestern University.

items.name: Archive ouverte
items.description: HAL (short for Hyper Articles en Ligne) is an open archive where authors can deposit scholarly documents from all academic fields.

items.name: Arias Montano
items.description: The Arias Montano Institutional Repository is the research repository of the University of Huelva (Spain), designed to collect, preserve, and disseminate the university’s scientific and educational outputs. It contains a wide range of digital resources, including publications, theses, teaching materials, and research datasets, supporting open access and long-term preservation of academic outputs. The repository also includes a specific collection for research data, allowing the storage and sharing of datasets generated by University of Huelva research groups and projects.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Arizona State University Research Data Repository
items.description:
The ASU Research Data Repository is a platform for ASU-affiliated researchers to share, preserve, and publish research data in a way that ensures long-term accessibility, usability, and citation. Our team supports researchers in preparing high-quality, well-documented datasets that comply with funder and publisher data sharing requirements.

Curated by ASU Library data professionals, the repository enables global discovery of research data through permanent digital identifiers (DOIs). It is powered by the open-source Dataverse application developed by Harvard University and complements the KEEP Institutional Repository to support the full range of ASU research outputs.
licences: Arizona State University Dataverse General Terms of Use
Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-BY) v1.0

items.name: ARP Research Data Repository
items.description: The HUN-REN Data Repository Platform (HUN-REN ARP) is a new repository infrastructure service that supports the continuous and long-term research data management of the entire HUN-REN research network. The development provides a solution for the secure digital storage, use and reuse of research data as a valuable data asset, as well as its further utilization by the research community and other sectors like the economy.

items.name: ARPHA Preprints
items.description: ARPHA Preprints provides a preprint (not peer-reviewed, not copyedited and not typeset versions of manuscripts) service for those manuscripts submitted to journals hosted on the ARPHA Platform that have selected this service. Preprints are optional, therefore authors need to confirm during submission whether they want their manuscript to be posted as a preprint. ARPHA Preprints is not open for direct submission of preprints, but only through the submission systems of the participating ARPHA journals. The scope and the article type of preprints are determined by those of the journal.

items.name: Artificial Intelligence-Ready CHEmiCal Knowledge Base
items.description: Artificial Intelligence-Ready CHEmiCal Knowledge Base (AIRCHECK) is an open, cloud-based platform that provides the high-quality, structured data AI needs to accelerate drug discovery. AIRCHECK helps researchers train and improve AI models to predict how small molecules interact with proteins.

items.name: ASEP
items.description: ASEP is an institutional data repository of the Czech Academy of Sciences, where data files with metadata (description) of authors of the Czech Academy of Sciences institutes are stored.

items.name: Aston Data Explorer
items.description: Aston Data Explorer is Aston University's repository for our research datasets.

items.name: Astromaterials Data System
items.description: The Astromaterials Data System is a NASA funded data infrastructure that supports the preservation, discovery, access and analysis of laboratory analytical data generated by the study of astromaterials samples. The Astromaterials Data System operates the Astromaterials Data Repository (AstroRepo), which archives, publishes and makes accessible data generated by the study of lunar samples (samples collected during the Apollo missions), meteorites, interstellar dust, solar wind, presolar grains, and other extraterrestrial materials. AstroRepo follows international best practices for trusted data repositories. The Astromaterials Data System is operated at the Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory of Columbia University as part of a suite of data systems for Earth and planetary sample data (chemical, mineralogical, and petrological observations), including EarthChem, the System for Earth Sample Registration, and the Library of Experimental Phase Relations.

items.name: Atlas of Open Science Resources
items.description: The Atlas of Open Science Resources (AZON 2.0) is a Polish multi-institutional, multidisciplinary repository led by Wrocław University of Science and Technology and several partner institutions. It provides open access to a broad range of scientific resources, including publications, research datasets, databases, multimedia, software-related files, and educational materials across fields such as engineering, medicine, life sciences, computer science, and the humanities.

items.name: ATTO Data Portal
items.description: The Amazon Tall Tower Observatory (ATTO) Data Portal is an interdisciplinary platform for storing, sharing, exchanging, and publishing data collected by the ATTO research consortium. Its core goal is to improve understanding of biogeochemical cycles and energy fluxes across the geosphere, biosphere, and atmosphere in the Amazon region and to feed that understanding into climate and Earth system models.

items.name: AuScope Data Repository
items.description: The AuScope Data Repository is dedicated to the preservation and continuous accessibility of geoscientific data generated by Australia's geoscience community, addressing fundamental geoscience inquiries and overarching challenges such as climate change, natural resource security, and natural hazards.

items.name: Beilstein Archives
items.description: This repository is currently limited to preprints related to the Beilstein Journal of Nanotechnology and the Beilstein Journal of Organic Chemistry.

items.name: Bialystok University of Technology Data Repository
items.description: The BUT Data Repository is the institutional research data repository of Bialystok University of Technology, designed to collect, preserve, and provide access to research data and scholarly outputs produced by its academic community.

items.name: Bicocca Open Archive Research Data
items.description: BOARD (Bicocca Open Archive Research Data) is the institutional data repository of the University of Milano-Bicocca. BOARD is an open, free-to-use research data repository, which enables members of University of Milano-Bicocca to make their research data publicly available. By depositing their research data in BOARD researchers can make their research data citable, share their data privately or publicly, ensure long-term storage for their data, keep access to all versions and link their article to their data.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Bilkent University Institutional Repository
items.description: The Bilkent University Institutional Repository (BUIR) is the open access digital repository of Bilkent University in Turkey, where the scholarly works of faculty, students, and researchers are collected, preserved, and made discoverable online. It includes academic publications, theses, dissertations, technical reports, and other research outputs from various departments across the university.

items.name: BindingDB database of measured binding affinities
items.description: BindingDB enables research by making a growing collection of high-quality, quantitative, protein-ligand binding data findable and usable. Funded by NIGMS/NIH.

items.name: Biological and Chemical Oceanography Data Management Office
items.description: The Biological and Chemical Oceanography Data Management Office (BCO-DMO) is a publicly accessible earth science data repository created to curate, publicly serve (publish), and archive digital data and information from biological, chemical and biogeochemical research conducted in coastal, marine, great lakes and laboratory environments. The BCO-DMO repository works closely with investigators funded through the NSF OCE Division’s Biological and Chemical Sections and the Division of Polar Programs Arctic Sciences and Antarctic Organisms & Ecosystems. The office provides services that span the full data life cycle, from data management planning support and DOI creation, to archive with appropriate national facilities.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Bioregistry
items.description: The Bioregistry is an open source, community curated registry, meta-registry, and compact identifier resolver.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Birkbeck Research Data Repository
items.description: The Birkbeck Research Data Repository (BiRD) is an institutional data archive managed by Birkbeck, University of London. It stores and preserves research datasets produced by the university’s academics and postgraduate researchers.

items.name: Bitbucket
items.description: Bitbucket is a Git-based source code repository hosting service owned by Atlassian. It provides a number of different access levels, from free through to premium paid services. Users can create public or private repositories, the latter of which is restricted to 5 users under the free plan.

items.name: bonndata
items.description: bonndata is the institutional, FAIR-aligned and curated, cross-disciplinary research data repository for the publication of research data for all researchers at the University of Bonn. The repository is fully embedded into the University IT and Data Center and curated by the Research Data Service Center (https://www.forschungsdaten.uni-bonn.de/en).
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Borealis, the Canadian Dataverse Repository
items.description:
Borealis, the Canadian Dataverse Repository, is a bilingual, multidisciplinary, secure, Canadian research data repository, supported by academic libraries and research institutions across Canada. Borealis supports open discovery, management, sharing, and preservation of Canadian research data. 

Borealis is a shared service provided in partnership with Canadian regional academic library consortia, institutions, research organizations, and the Digital Research Alliance of Canada, with technical infrastructure hosted by Scholars Portal and the University of Toronto Libraries. Borealis is designed to balance openness and responsibility, following the principle of “as open as possible, as closed as necessary.” While metadata is openly discoverable, access to data may be restricted where appropriate. Deposit is limited to affiliated researchers, faculty, and students from participating institutions, ensuring institutional oversight and compliance with policy requirements.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: BORIS Portal
items.description: BORIS Portal allows researchers at the University of Bern to publish publications, research data, and information on projects and funding. It also supports the publication of software and other digital items, audiovisual materials, and theses.

items.name: Brandeis ScholarWorks
items.description: Brandeis ScholarWorks is the institutional research repository and scholarly portal of Brandeis University. It preserves and provides access to a wide range of research and creative outputs, including publications, datasets, theses and dissertations, reports, multimedia, and other scholarly works produced by the Brandeis community. The platform also supports the discovery and dissemination of Brandeis research through researcher profiles and searchable collections.

items.name: Bridge of Knowledge - Open Research Data Repository
items.description: Bridge of Knowledge - Open Research Data Repository collects data and metadata for long-term preservation from Gdańsk University of Technology, Medical University of Gdańsk and the University of Gdańsk. To ensure reusability of archived resources the available research data are described by standards developed by dedicated, experienced scientific team. The metadata allow other external computer systems to interpret the collected data. ORD descriptions will also include data reuse or reduction scenarios to facilitate further processing. This provides researchers with the ability to meet requirements regarding research data management and dissemination set by funding agencies, publishers, and also institutional and national authorities.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Bridges
items.description: Bridges is a collaborative digital repository for Monash University researchers. It allows researchers to manage, store, share and selectively publish their research files as citable research outputs with a persistent URL. Researchers maintain control over who can see their private files and all uploads are stored at Monash University.
licences: Monash University Library Terms and Conditions

items.name: British Columbia Data Catalogue
items.description: The BC Data Catalogue is the place to find B.C. Government data, applications and web services. Government ministries and many broader public sector agencies publish their data resources in the Catalogue.

items.name: Brown Digital Repository
items.description: The Brown Digital Repository is the institutional digital repository of Brown University, designed to gather, index, preserve, and provide access to a wide range of digital scholarly assets produced by the university community. It includes research datasets, publications, digital collections, media, and other scholarly or creative digital objects that support teaching, research, and institutional activities.

items.name: CaltechDATA
items.description: CaltechDATA is an institutional data repository for Caltech. Caltech library runs the repository to preserve the accomplishments of Caltech researchers and share their results with the world. Caltech-associated researchers can upload data, link data with their publications, and assign a permanent DOI so that others can reference the data set. The repository also preserves software and has automatic Github integration. All files present in the repository are open access or embargoed, and all metadata is always available to the public.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Canadian Laboratory Initiative on Pediatric Reference Interval Database
items.description: The CALIPER Database is a specialized medical database that provides age-, sex-, and ethnicity-specific reference intervals for laboratory test results in children and adolescents. Developed through a nationwide Canadian research initiative led by The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), it contains data from over 12,000 healthy participants and covers more than 200 biochemical, hematological, immunological, and endocrine markers. The database helps healthcare professionals accurately interpret pediatric laboratory results and improve the diagnosis and monitoring of childhood diseases.

items.name: Canadian Urban Data Catalogue
items.description: The Canadian Urban Data Catalogue (CUDC) is an open urban data repository created to foster, promote, and facilitate access to datasets for the urban data domain. CUDC stores metadata about each dataset in the repository to increase awareness amongst urban researchers. It brings city administrators, citizens, and academic research centres together to enhance local communities by promoting collaboration and innovation toward building digital city infrastructures.

items.name: Cardiff University Research Data Repository
items.description:
The Cardiff University Research Data Repository is an institutional platform powered by Figshare and dedicated to the preservation, curation, and dissemination of research outputs produced by Cardiff University. It supports the university’s Open Research commitment and ensures compliance with major funder mandates by providing a stable environment for long-term data accessibility.

The repository is multidisciplinary, hosting datasets, software, and media across all research domains. Every public output is assigned a DataCite DOI to facilitate formal citation and persistent discovery. Managed by the University Library Service, the platform enables FAIR principles through attributes such as standardized metadata, support for open-access licenses, and the provision of "metadata-only" records for restricted or sensitive datasets.

items.name: Central Repository ICTM
items.description: CeR i.e. Central Repository ICTM is a digital repository of the Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy, University of Belgrade, Serbia. CeR provides open access to the publications, as well as to other outputs of the research projects implemented in this institution.

items.name: CERES Research Repository
items.description: CERES is the Cranfield Collection of E-Research, the institutional digital repository of Cranfield University for storing and providing access to the university’s research outputs. It includes a wide range of scholarly materials such as journal articles, conference papers, theses, book chapters, technical reports, and associated research data.

items.name: Chemotion repository
items.description: The Chemotion-repository is a repository for chemistry research data. The repository was founded at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) in Germany as a project funded by the German Research Foundation. The repository is domain specific, offering diverse functions to save and work with chemical datasets and analyse files. The DOI generation is provided by DataCite. The repository supports the storage of data related to chemical samples or reactions, with a focus on data from synthetic and analytical work. Data can be uploaded directly to the repository or can be added via a connector that mediates the transfer of data from the chemotion ELN (available as an Open Source) to the repository. Chemotion repository is part of the strategy of the National Research Data Infrastructure for Chemistry (NFDI4Chem). Hints and explanations for the use of the repository are available in the documentation: https://www.chemotion.net/docs/repo/

items.name: ChemTHEATRE
items.description: ChemTHEATRE is an online resource for browsing and analyzing curated and user-contributed data sets of environmental contaminants. ChemTHEATRE also stores metadata of the samples and of the experimental methods.

items.name: Cherry Repository
items.description: CHERRY, ie CHEmistry RepositoRY is a joint digital repository of the all departments in University of Belgrade - Faculty of Chemistry. CHERRY provides open access to the publications, as well as to other outputs of the research projects implemented in this institution.

items.name: China National GeneBank DataBase
items.description:
The China National GeneBank database (CNGBdb) is a unified platform for biological big data sharing and application services. At present, CNGBdb has integrated a large amount of internal and external biological data from resources such as CNGB, NCBI, and the EBI. There are a number of sub databases in CNGBdb, including literature, variation, gene, genome, protein, sequence, organism, project, sample, experiment, run, and assembly. Based on underlying big data and cloud computing technologies, it provides various data services, including archive, analysis, knowledge search, management authorization of biological data. CNGBdb adopts data structures and standards of international omics, health, and medicine, such as The International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration (INSDC), The Global Alliance for Genomics and Health GA4GH (GA4GH), Global Genome Biodiversity Network (GGBN), American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG), and constructs standardized data and structures with wide compatibility. All public data and data services provided by CNGBdb are freely available to all users worldwide.
CNGB Sequence Archive (CNSA) is the bionomics data repository of CNGBdb.
CNGB Sequence Archive (CNSA) is a convenient and efficient archiving system of multi-omics data in life science, which provides archiving services for raw sequencing reads and further analyzed results. CNSA follows the international data standards for omics data, and supports online and batch submission of multiple data types such as Project, Sample, Experiment/Run, Assembly, Variation, Metabolism, Single cell, and Sequence. Moreover, CNSA has achieved the correlation of sample entities, sample information, and analyze data on some projects. Its data submission service can be used as a supplement to the literature publishing process to support early data sharing.

items.name: City of Brantford Open Data Catalogue
items.description: The City of Brantford Open Data Catalogue is an open municipal data portal that provides free access to a wide range of datasets published by the City of Brantford, Canada. It includes information about local government services, infrastructure, transportation, environment, parks, and more in machine‑readable formats for analysis and application development.

items.name: City of Grand Prairie Open Data Portal
items.description: The City of Grande Prairie Open Data Portal is a public platform that offers free access to a variety of the city’s datasets.

items.name: City of Kamloops Open Data Catalog
items.description: The City of Kamloops Open Data Catalog is hosted on ArcGIS Hub, offering free access to a wide variety of municipal geospatial and tabular datasets. It allows users to browse, download, and use data on topics like parks, infrastructure, water systems, and administrative boundaries to support transparency and civic engagement.

items.name: City of Victoria Open Data Portal
items.description: The City of Victoria’s Open Data Portal allows you to explore and download open data, discover and analyze datasets using maps, and develop new web and mobile applications.

items.name: CNRS Research Data
items.description:
As part of the Research Data plan, the CNRS Research Data institutional repository offers CNRS scientists and their collaborators a solution for sharing data when there is no thematic or institutional repository adapted to their research field. CNRS Research Data provides a space in which depositors can share and promote data (legally disseminable, completed, documented and reusable) produced or co-produced as part of research work supported by the CNRS.
CNRS Research Data includes a generic main collection and laboratory collections that can be created on demand. The submission is done directly by the scientists and a team of moderators then assists them from the curation of the dataset to its publication.
licences: Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODC ODbL) v1.0

items.name: Code Ocean
items.description: Code Ocean is a cloud-based computational reproducibility platform that provides researchers and developers an easy way to share, discover and run code published in academic journals and conferences. The platform provides open access to the published software code and data to view and download for everyone for free. Users can execute all published code without installing anything on their personal computer. Everything runs in the cloud on CPUs or GPUs according to the user needs.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Coherent X-ray Imaging Data Bank
items.description: The Coherent X-ray Imaging Data Bank (CXIDB) offers scientists from all over the world a unique opportunity to access data from Coherent X-ray Imaging (CXI) experiments. It arose from the need to share the terabytes of data generated from X-ray free-electron laser experiments although it caters to all light sources. Accessibility is crucial not only to make efficient use of experimental facilities, but also to improve the reproducibility of results and enable new research based on previous experiments.
subjects: Atomic, Molecular, Optical and Plasma Physics
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: COlleCtion of Open Natural prodUcTs
items.description: COCONUT (COlleCtion of Open Natural prodUcTs) is a large, open-access database of natural products compiled from multiple open data sources into a unified resource. It provides standardized chemical structures along with curated metadata to facilitate research and computational analysis.

items.name: Cork Open Research Archive
items.description: Cork Open Research Archive (CORA) is University College Cork’s Open Access institutional repository which enables UCC researchers to make their research outputs freely available and accessible.

items.name: Coscine
items.description: Coscine is a platform for research data management (RDM) that is being developed at RWTH Aachen University. Researchers from all fields can create projects there, store data including the associated metadata, share it with other project members and archive the research data for ten years after the project in accordance with good scientific practice. The metadata is stored using so-called application profiles. Coscine enables compliance with the FAIR principles by bundling research data, metadata, interfaces and PIDs in a linked data set according to the "FAIR Digital Objects" model. Coscine's functions can be accessed both via the web interface and via APIs, enabling automated processes.

items.name: CRC 1625 RDMS
items.description:
Collaborative Research Center (CRC) 1625: Atomic-scale understanding and design of multifunctional compositionally complex solid solution surfaces.

Compositionally complex solid solutions (CCSS) comprising five or more different elements mixed in a simple single-phase crystal structure provide conceptually unique, highly promising prospects in important scientific and technological areas, where the surface dominates properties such as – and ultimately not limited to –electrocatalysis and corrosion, crucial for future sustainable energy conversion systems.

The CRC aims to leverage the possibilities of CCSS as material design platforms by establishing a combined theoretical and experimental understanding of their atomic-scale surface features, as the unique properties of CCSS are caused by the large number of diverse poly-elemental active sites across their surface. Gaining control of and the ability to design these surface atom arrangements (SAA) has the potential to overcome limitations of conventional electrocatalysts and will pave the way to multifunctional materials, with unprecedented combinations of activity and stability as well as possibilities for cascade reactions. SAA are specific arrangements of (sub)surface atoms and their chemical identities. They form in statistical abundance the surface composition of CCSS. Knowledge of SAA is essential for designing composition-structure‑activity relations for CCSS surfaces.

The CRC aims to understand and control SAA – their formation, their variation for different systems and compositions, changes in SAA due to experimental conditions – to systematically tailor and manipulate them to design their properties. Development of new catalysts is not the primary goal; rather, advancement in fundamental understanding and exploration of new opportunities offered by SAA of CCSS. Initially, noble metal thin films will be used as model CCSS as their oxidation resistance supports SAA identification. Gaining detailed insights into the dependence of reaction mechanisms on the SAA and the understanding of CCSS surface metallurgy will then enable the design of multifunctional and sustainable electrocatalysts. This multi-dimensional challenge will be addressed by a fully interdisciplinary team (materials science, surface science, physics, chemistry, data science) using high-throughput methods in atomistic simulation, synthesis, characterisation, electrochemical probing, and in-depth experiments towards atomic-scale resolution. SAA determine electrochemical reactions on the atomic scale which is addressed by theory and atomic-scale characterisation. However, this atomistic view needs to be combined with the high-dimensional composition-property space of SAA and CCSS. Using materials informatics, we will integrate all data across scales and research areas, establish data-guided workflows, extract knowledge from data and organise it in knowledge graphs. Our holistic approach will be used to fulfil the vision of the CRC to control SAA on the atomic scale and across the surface and enable the design of ideal CCSS surfaces for specific applications.
subjects: Atomic, Molecular, Optical and Plasma Physics

items.description: The Crystallography Open Database (COD) is a project that aims to gather all available inorganic, metal-organic and small organic molecule structural data in one database.
domains: X-ray crystallography 3D molecular structure determination assay
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: CU Scholar
items.description: CU Scholar is an open access institutional repository supporting the research and teaching mission of the University of Colorado Boulder. It is intended to serve as a platform for preserving and providing perpetual public access to the research activities of members of the CU Boulder community.

items.name: CUHK Research Data Repository
items.description: The CUHK Research Data Repository is an open institutional research data platform run by The Chinese University of Hong Kong that lets researchers deposit, preserve, and share their research datasets.

items.name: CyVerse Data Common Repository
items.description: The Data Commons provides services to manage, organize, preserve, publish, discover, and reuse data. Using our pipelines, you can easily publish data to the NCBI or directly to the CyVerse Data Commons. CyVerse Curated Data are stable and have DOIs. Community Released Data are maintained by community members and may not be permanent.

items.name: Dados.UPB
items.description: The data repository of the Universidade Politécnica de Bragança (Bragança Polytechnic University) aims to store, preserve and make available research data generated by the academic community, in open access - as open as possible, as closed as necessary.

items.name: DaKS - University of Kassel's research data repository
items.description: DaKS is the institutional repository of the University of Kassel for research data. It offers structured storage of research data alongside with descriptive metadata, long-term archiving for at least 10 years and – if requested – the publication of the dataset with a DOI.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: DALIA
items.description: DALIA (Open Data from the Bologna Area Library) is an archive of digital data and its metadata catalogue, which brings together the digital data that the Dario Nobili Library of the CNR Territorial Area of Bologna has produced and/or acquired in the course of its activities and projects over the last 20 years and is constantly growing.

items.name: DANS Data Station Life Sciences
items.description: Domain-specific data repository for the Life Sciences, covering all disciplines from the health, medical as well as the green life sciences. This repository primarily serves research communities in The Netherlands, but is open to international researchers and projects that carry a connection to The Netherlands or Dutch research themes, institutes and programmes. The repository is part of the global Dataverse project, and through the interaction of DANS with the larger Dataverse community as wel as the participation in major national and European infrastructural data projects, the repository is continuously improved and enhanced.
licences: Data Archiving and Networked Services (DANS) Privacy Policy

items.name: Danube University Open Online Repository
items.description: The DOOR (Danube University Open Online Repository) is the institutional repository of the University for Continuing Education Krems (Austria), designed for the long-term preservation, management, and dissemination of digital research outputs. It provides access to scientific publications, research data, educational resources, and other digital materials produced by the university community. The repository supports open access by assigning persistent identifiers (DOIs) and enabling the sharing of research outputs with the scientific community. DOOR covers multiple disciplines and serves as a platform for researchers and staff of the University for Continuing Education Krems to archive and publish their work.

items.name: DaRUS
items.description: DaRUS, the data repository of the University of Stuttgart, offers a secure location for research data and codes, be it for the administration of own data, for exchange within a research group, for sharing with selected partners or for publishing.

items.name: Data MB
items.description: Data MB is Manitoba's government open data portal, providing public access to government datasets. It reflects the province’s commitment to transparency and accountability by making information available online. The platform is continuously updated as new datasets are released.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Data Repository for the University of Minnesota
items.description: Data Repository for the University of Minnesota (DRUM) is a publicly available collection of digital research data generated by U of M researchers, students, and staff. Anyone can search and download the data housed in the repository, instantly or by request. DRUM accepts submissions from University affiliates for digital archiving and access.

items.name: Data Repository of the CAS Scientific Data General Center
items.description: The Data Repository of the CAS Scientific Data General Center is an institutional research data repository supporting the publication, preservation, discovery, citation, and reuse of scientific datasets. It provides services for data submission, metadata management, data access, persistent identification, and data sharing.

items.name: data.bris Research Data Repository
items.description: The data.bris Research Data Repository is an online digital repository of multi-disciplinary research datasets produced at the University of Bristol. The University of Bristol’s mission is to pursue and share knowledge and understanding, both for their own sake and to help individuals and society fulfil their potential. The University is research-intensive, supporting both individual scholarship and interdisciplinary or thematic research of the highest quality. The Research Data Repository offers a means for Bristol’s researchers to share research data openly and with restricted access. Data.bris is maintained by the University of Bristol Research Data Service.

items.name: data.eNanoMapper.net
items.description: data.eNanoMapper.net is a public database hosting nanomaterials characterization data and biological and toxicological information. The database provides various possibilities to search and explore information, and to download data in various standard formats. The database supports data upload through configurable Excel templates.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

organisations.name: Community Research and Development Information Service
Community Research and Development Information Service

items.name: Data.gov.au
items.description: Data.gov.au is the central source of Australian open government data. Anyone can access the public data published by federal, state and local government agencies.

items.name: Data.gov.uk Directory
items.description: data.gov.uk is the United Kingdom government’s official open data catalogue, providing public access to thousands of non-personal datasets published by central government, local authorities, and public bodies. The platform makes diverse data on topics like health, transport, crime, economy, environment, and government spending searchable and reusable.

items.name: data.world
items.description: data.world is a repository for open-access data sets. Their goal is to build the most meaningful, collaborative, and abundant data resource in the world.
licences: Community Data License Agreement - Permissive, v1.0 (CDLA-Permissive-1.0)
Community Data License Agreement - Sharing, v1.0.

items.name: DataCite Repository
items.description: DataCite is a leading global non-profit organisation that provides persistent identifiers (DOIs) for research data. Their goal is to help the research community locate, identify, and cite research data with confidence. They support the creation and allocation of DOIs and accompanying metadata. They provide services that support the enhanced search and discovery of research content. They also promote data citation and advocacy through community-building efforts and responsive communication and outreach materials. DataCite gathers metadata for each DOI assigned to an object. The metadata is used for a large index of research data that can be queried directly to find data, obtain stats and explore connections. All the metadata is free to access and review. To showcase and expose the metadata gathered, DataCite provides an integrated search interface, where it is possible to search, filter and extract all the details from a collection of millions of records.

items.name: DataDOI
items.description: DataDOI is the institutional research data repository of the University of Tartu Library. It preserves and disseminates Estonian research data across all fields, ensuring it is findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable in line with FAIR principles.

items.name: DataON Repository
items.description: DataON is an inclusive national research data platform established by KISTI that spans a comprehensive range of disciplines—from engineering, physical sciences, life sciences, health, environment, earth sciences, AI, materials, energy, and chemistry, to humanities and social sciences. It aggregates global repository metadata and registers datasets produced by government-funded research based on Korea’s national science and technology classification system, which explicitly includes both scientific/technical fields and the humanities/social sciences.

items.name: DataRepositoriUM
items.description: Data Repository of the University of Minho to share, publish and manage research data from University of Minho research units.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: DataSpace@HKUST
items.description: DataSpace@HKUST serves primarily as a data repository for HKUST researchers. Faculty members, staff, and research postgraduate students can use the platform to store, share, organize, preserve, and publish their research data.

items.name: DataSTORRE
items.description: DataStorre is an online digital repository of multi-disciplinary research datasets produced at the University of Stirling.

items.name: Dataverse at University of Milan
items.description:
Data@UNIMI is University of Milan's Research Data Repository, based on Dataverse - open source repository software built by Harvard University. The objective of Dataverse  service is to enable research data deposit, management, search, sharing and reuse.  When the researchers deposit their research data in BOARD, they will effectively make their research data public and citable, share their data, ensure long-term preservation, and implement an effective versioning policy. 

All deposited Datasets have necessary metadata that facilitates discoverability.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: DataverseNL
items.description: DataverseNL provides online storage, sharing and registration of research data, during the research period and after its completion. DataverseNL is a shared service provided by participating institutions and DANS. DataverseNL uses the Dataverse software developed by Harvard University, which is used worldwide.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: DataverseNO
items.description: DataverseNO (https://dataverse.no/) is a national, generalist repository for open research data, operated and coordinated by UiT The Arctic University of Norway. DataverseNO is a curated and FAIR-enabling repository. The technical infrastructure of the repository is based on the open-source application Dataverse, which is developed by an international developer and user community led by Harvard University. DataverseNO is CoreTrustSeal certified.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: DAT’AMU
items.description: The Aix-Marseille University Dataverse (AMU Dataverse) is the institutional research data repository of Aix-Marseille University (AMU), hosted on the French national research data repository Recherche Data Gouv platform. It enables researchers to deposit, preserve, describe, and share research datasets with persistent identifiers (DOIs) to support data reuse and open science. The repository covers a wide range of disciplines represented at AMU and provides long-term access to research data produced by the university community.

items.name: Deep Blue Data
items.description: Deep Blue Data is a repository offered by the University of Michigan Library that provides access and preservation services for digital research data that were developed or used in the support of research activities at U-M.

items.name: DeiC Dataverse
items.description:
DeiC Dataverse is the Danish National Repository for Research Data. It allows researchers to publish and archive their research data in line with the FAIR principles, including metadata descriptions, DOI’s (Digital Object Identifiers) as persistent identifiers and clearly defined terms and conditions for access and reuse. 

DeiC Dataverse is owned by the Danish e-infrastructure Consortium, DeiC, and provided free of charge to all Danish research institutions.

items.name: depositar
items.description: depositar — taking the term from the Portuguese/Spanish verb for to deposit — is an online repository for research data. The site is built by the researchers for the researchers. You are free to deposit, discover, and reuse datasets on depositar for all your research purposes.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication
Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODC ODbL) v1.0

items.name: DepositOnce
items.description: DepositOnce is TU Berlin’s institutional repository and is operated and continually developed by the Service Center for Research Data and Publications.

items.name: Diamond DataGateway
items.description: The Diamond DataGateway provides access to experimental data generated at the facility’s beamlines, including raw data, processed datasets, and associated metadata from user proposals and investigations. These datasets cover a wide range of scientific disciplines such as physics, chemistry, biology, and materials science, and may include files like diffraction patterns, spectroscopy measurements, imaging data, and structural analysis results.

items.name: Digital Academic Archives and Repositories
items.description: The Digital Academic Archives and Repositories (DABAR) is a repository for Croatia's education and science institutions' digital assets, i.e., various digital objects produced by the institutions and their employees. DABAR stores these digital assets in institutional and thematic digital repositories and archives accessible within and maintained by DABAR itself.

items.name: Digital Commons Data - Babeș-Bolyai University
items.description: Digital Commons Data at Babeș-Bolyai University in Cluj-Napoca (DCD-UBB) is an institutional data repository for faculty, staff, and students, hosting datasets supporting research and publishing activities. Registration with the repository is available with UBB institutional credentials, and the dataset submission process is moderated by UBB data curators. Users do not need to register in order to access hosted datasets, but embargo settings by authors might prevent full access to all content. Please refer to this webpage for further information and resources on the use of DCD-UBB and the related institutional policies: https://csu.centre.ubbcluj.ro/osd/resurse/documentatie-repozitorii/

items.name: Digital Commons Data UniCatt
items.description: Digital Commons UniCatt - DCD UniCatt - is the institutional repository for faculty and researchers of the Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore to share their research data and supporting files, in compliance with funder and publisher policies and according to the recommendations set forth by the FAIR Principles for Open Science. Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore has two other repositories for its scientific publications: IRIS UniCatt and PubliRES, the University's portal of scientific publications and researchers' expertise.

items.name: Digital Porous Media Portal
items.description: The Digital Porous Media Portal allows fast storage and retrieval, sharing, organization and analysis of images of varied porous micro-structures. This portal (formerly known as Digital Rocks Portal) enhances research resources for modeling/prediction of porous material properties in the fields of Petroleum, Civil and Environmental Engineering and Geology. It lets users manage, preserve, visualize and analyze available images of porous materials and experiments performed on them, and any accompanying measurements (porosity, capillary pressure, permeability, electrical, NMR and elastic properties, etc.) required for both validation on modeling approaches and the upscaling and building of larger (hydro)geological models.
licences: Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-BY) v1.0

items.name: Digital Repository at the University of Maryland
items.description: DRUM (Digital Repository at the University of Maryland) is the University of Maryland’s institutional repository that collects, preserves, and provides public access to the institution’s scholarly output, including research articles, theses, dissertations, and datasets. It enables faculty, researchers, and students to share their work globally and ensures long-term preservation.

items.name: Digital Repository of the University of Beira Interior
items.description: The uBibliorum - Institutional Repository of the University of Beira Interior (UBI) is an essential tool in the pursuit of its mission as a Higher Education institution and aims to gather, publicise and preserve, in a single site, all the scientific production carried out at UBI. This repository is intended to capture, distribute and preserve digital research products produced by members of UBI.

items.name: Digital State Library of Upper Austria
items.description: The Digital State Library of Upper Austria is a digital library providing online access to digitized historical and regional publications held by the Upper Austrian State Library. Its collection includes rare books, manuscripts, periodicals, maps, and other historical documents, with a particular focus on works related to Upper Austria. The digitized materials are available for browsing, full-text searching, and, where permitted, downloading. The platform preserves and improves access to valuable historical and cultural heritage materials for researchers and the general public.

items.name: DIGITUM
items.description: DIGITUM is the University of Murcia’s Institutional Digital Repository. Its goal is to provide open access to the University’s scientific and academic output, to increase the visibility of its content, and to ensure the preservation of these digital archives.

items.name: Dipòsit Digital de Documents de la UAB
items.description: The DDD (UAB Digital Document Repository) is the platform through which the university’s research, teaching, and institutional output is collected, managed, disseminated, and preserved. It also includes digital documents that are part of the UAB libraries' collections or that complement them. It offers an organised, open-access, and interoperable collection.

items.name: Discover
items.description: The Discover platform offers access to research data from projects related to LMU Munich. It provides a one-stop search entry point and enables a targeted search for relevant research data. Discover is an important resource for researchers and students, allowing them to access a wide range of data covering the broad spectrum of research at LMU Munich.

items.name: Discovery
items.description: Discovery is the institutional research portal of the University of Dundee. It was originally created in 2010 to provide an institutional repository and digital preservation service for research material created by the University of Dundee community. Since then it has evolved into a comprehensive source of information on all aspects of the University’s commitment to research, and forms a key part of its Research Information System (Pure). A key area of Discovery is its repository of research outputs, comprising links to electronic full text of peer-reviewed articles and conference papers, as well as book chapters, theses and other forms of written research from the University of Dundee’s academic staff and postgraduate students. Some publications are also available as full-text downloads where copyright restrictions permit. Discovery also holds “grey literature”, such as working and discussion papers, technical reports and preprints. In addition, research datasets, sound and image collections, multimedia, software and other forms of research data can be deposited.

items.name: DMU Figshare
items.description: DMU Figshare is the institutional research data repository of De Montfort University (DMU), UK, designed to store, preserve, and share research outputs in accordance with open research principles. It provides access to a wide range of research materials, including datasets, experimental data, survey data, images, genomic data, measurement data, and other digital research outputs. The repository supports multidisciplinary research across areas such as humanities, social sciences, life sciences, natural sciences, and engineering.

items.name: Docker Hub
items.description: Docker Hub is a library and community for sharing container images. It currently contains over 100,000 container images from software vendors, open-source projects, and the community. It has become a common way of sharing bioinformatics tools and resources in a way that reduces the difficulty of running these tools in a compute environment with the correct software dependencies.

items.name: DOE CODE
items.description: The Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Scientific and Technical Information (OSTI) provides a DOE software services platform and search tool for DOE-funded code – DOE CODE. DOE CODE provides functionality for development collaboration, submission of software/code to OSTI, software/code archiving and preservation, and discovery of scientific and business software.

items.name: Domus Dados
items.description: Domus Dados is the research data repository of the Federal University of São Paulo (UNIFESP), providing a platform for storing, preserving, and sharing research datasets generated by the university community. It supports open science by making research data discoverable and citable, using persistent identifiers and standard metadata practices.

items.name: DR-NTU (Data)
items.description:
DR-NTU (Data) is an institutional research data repository of Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore. 
The repository has a mission to curate, store, preserve, make available and enable the download of digital data generated by the NTU research community in various disciplines. The repository develops and provides guidance for managing, sharing, and reusing research data to promote responsible data sharing in support of open science and research integrity.
licences: DR-NTU (Data) User Guides and Policies: General Terms of Use

items.name: Dryad Digital Repository
items.description:
Dryad is a non-profit open data publishing platform and a community, committed to the open availability and routine re-use of all research data. Dryad publishes data in all forms and formats, spanning all areas of research, under a CC0 license. A "private for peer review" option allows authors to share data with editors and reviewers prior to publication, it they wish.

Dryad datasets undergo a quality control screening. Experienced professional curators review each submission to ensure compliance with FAIR data standards, and work directly with authors on any revisions to ensure that their data meets publisher and funder requirements.

Institutions, publishers, societies, and other organizations partner with Dryad to sponsor the cost of data publication for affiliated researchers. All fees are set on a cost-recovery basis.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Duke Research Data Repository
items.description: The Research Data Repository is a service of the Duke University Libraries that provides curation, access, and preservation of research data produced by the Duke community. The Duke Research Data Repository accepts data, documentation, software, and other code related to the teaching and research mission of Duke University, including data linked to a publication, research project, and/or class projects. Data deposit is open to all members of the Duke Community with a valid netid. All data are openly accessible for direct download. All data go through a curation process to help ensure data are well described, in a structure and format that supports long-term preservation, and generally meet the FAIR Guiding Principles for data (i.e., Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable). All data and documentation are openly accessible for download unless under embargo.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Durham University Research Data Repository
items.description: This is the University's institutional research data repository.  It contains the research datasets that support the findings in our research papers and other outputs.

items.name: e-cienciaDatos
items.description: e-cienciaDatos is a multidisciplinary data repository that houses the scientific datasets of researchers from the public universities of the Community of Madrid and the UNED, members of the Consorcio Madroño, in order to give visibility to these data. The purpose of this repository is to ensure data preservation and to facilitate data access and reuse. e-cienciaDatos collects datasets from of each of the member universities. e-cienciaDatos offers the deposit and publication of datasets, assigning a digital object identifier DOI to each of them. The association of a dataset with a DOI will facilitate data verification, dissemination, reuse, impact and long-term access. In addition, the repository provides a standardized citation for each dataset, which contains sufficient information so that it can be identified and located, including the DOI.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: e-space
items.description: The Manchester Metropolitan University Repository (e-space) is the institutional repository of Manchester Metropolitan University, designed to preserve, showcase, and provide access to the University's research outputs. It hosts a wide range of scholarly materials, including publications, theses, and research datasets, ensuring their long-term preservation and discoverability. The repository supports open research by assigning persistent identifiers where appropriate and enabling researchers to share their work in compliance with institutional and funder policies.

items.name: EarthChem
items.description: EarthChem develops and maintains databases, software, and services that support the preservation, discovery, access and analysis of geochemical data, and facilitate their integration with the broad array of other available earth science parameters. The EarthChem Portal stores geochemical data, provides a variety of search, visualization, and output formatting options, and is interoperable with the LEPR database and the MELTS software. EarthChem Library is a data repository that archives, publishes and makes accessible data and other digital content from geoscience research.

items.name: EBAS
items.description: EBAS is a database hosting observation data of atmospheric chemical composition and physical properties. EBAS hosts data submitted by data originators in support of a number of national and international programs ranging from monitoring activities to research projects. EBAS is developed and operated by the Norwegian Institute for Air Research (NILU).

items.name: eCommons
items.description: eCommons is a service of the Cornell University Library that provides long-term access to a broad range of Cornell-related digital content of enduring value. Content types include: pre- and post-publication papers, technical reports, theses and dissertations, books, lectures and presentations, datasets, digital departmental newsletters, administrative reports, compilations of University data, and meeting agendas and minutes. Content produced by others but of research and/or teaching value may also be appropriate for eCommons. Such material is normally solicited, collected, or identified by Cornell faculty, researchers, staff, and students, who then arrange all necessary clearances needed to deposit the material. Examples of such content include: datasets, electronic books and multimedia, presentations given at Cornell events, digitized research materials.

items.name: eCrystals
items.description: eCrystals is the archive for Crystal Structures generated by the Southampton Chemical Crystallography Group and the EPSRC UK National Crystallography Service. It contains all the fundamental and derived data resulting from a single crystal X-ray structure determination, but excluding the raw images.
domains: X-ray crystallography 3D molecular structure determination assay
licences: Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-BY) v1.0

items.name: eData
items.description: eData is an institutional repository where STFC staff can deposit data and software that support journal articles and other published research. It offers a service for the deposit, registration, preservation, discovery, sharing and citation of these digital objects. eData does not replace subject-based, national, or STFC Facility data repositories already in use, such as ICAT. Researchers should check with their funder or facility for any specific requirements on where to deposit data or software.

items.name: Edinburgh DataShare
items.description: Edinburgh DataShare is a digital repository of research data produced at the University of Edinburgh, hosted by Information Services. Edinburgh University researchers who have produced research data associated with an existing or forthcoming publication, or which has potential use for other researchers, are invited to upload their dataset for sharing and safekeeping. A persistent identifier and suggested citation will be provided. CoreTrustSeal certification was first received in January 2022.
licences: Edinburgh DataShare Data and Metadata Usage Policy

items.name: edoc-Server
items.description: edoc is the Open Access publication server and institutional repository of Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin. It provides long-term access to the university’s scholarly publications and research data, including articles, theses, books, datasets, images, audio and video files, models, and software. The repository supports the dissemination and preservation of research outputs across the university’s diverse academic disciplines.

items.name: EELS Data Base
items.description: The EELS Data Base is a compilation of valence and core-loss spectra from Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy experiments and X-Ray spectra.
licences: Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODC ODbL) v1.0

items.name: EGI Applications Database
items.description: The EGI Applications Database (AppDB) is service which stores and provides information about software solutions in the form of native software products, virtual appliances, and containers, the programmers and scientists involved, and publications derived from the registered solutions.
licences: GNU Affero General Public License (AGPL) v3.0 only

items.name: Emissions of atmospheric Compounds and Compilation of Ancillary Data
items.description: Emissions of atmospheric Compounds and Compilation of Ancillary Data (ECCAD) aims at providing scientific users with an easy access to a large number of existing datasets on surface emissions of atmospheric compounds at the global and regional scales. Data manipulation tools as well as statistical information over the different regions (climatic regions, continents, oceans, OECD regions, etc.) are also available for users.

items.name: EMODnet Biology
items.description: EMODnet Biology provides free access to data and products on temporal and spatial distribution of marine species and species traits from all European regional seas. EMODnet Biology is part of the EU funded European Marine Observation and Data Network.

items.name: Energy Data eXchange
items.description: EDX is the Department of Energy (DOE)/Fossil Energy's (FE) virtual library and data laboratory built to find, connect, curate, use and re-use data to advance fossil energy and environmental R&D. EDX provides (1) long-term curation of both historic and current data and information from a wide variety of sources, (2) access to research across multiple NETL projects and programs and energy science needs, (3) discovery of data and information, including technical products from NETL-affiliated research, and (4) support for collaboration and coordination between various agencies, organizations, and institutions through EDX’s Collaborative Workspaces. EDX has both public and private aspects to facilitate external and internal access to research. The public side of EDX supports discovery and access to publicly available data from NETL as well as open-access data from authoritative, external sources. The private side of EDX supports research collaboration and coordination using role-based security privileges and access rights.

items.name: Enlighten: Research Data
items.description:
Enlighten: Research Data is the institutional repository for the University of Glasgow, designed to provide a long-term, stable environment for the deposit, discovery, and curation of research data outputs produced by its academic community. The repository supports the University’s commitment to Open Science and compliance with major funder mandates by ensuring that research data is preserved and made available for reuse where possible.

Built on the EPrints platform and integrated with the DataCite infrastructure, Enlighten: Research Data assigns Persistent Identifiers (DOIs) to all datasets to facilitate citation and tracking of impact. The repository is multidisciplinary, hosting a wide range of data types across the life sciences, physical sciences, social sciences, and humanities. It emphasises the creation of high-quality metadata records, allowing for "metadata-only" entries in cases where data are deposited in external repositories or where data must remain restricted due to commercial, ethical, or legal constraints.

The service is managed by the University of Glasgow Research Information Management team.

items.name: Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory User Data Portal
items.description: The EMSL NEXUS User Portal supports the management, sharing, and reporting of BER user facility data generated onsite by users and User organizations. EMSL is one of the 28 U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science user facilities. EMSL is housed on the campus of Pacific Northwest National Laboratory in Richland, Washington. DOE’s Biological and Environmental Research (BER) program supports EMSL and several other user facilities who are conducting research related to the fundamental understanding and prediction of complex biological, Earth, and environmental systems for energy and infrastructure security. As a user facility, EMSL provides shared laboratory resources, instrumentation, and expertise to the scientific community. Access to EMSL resources is determined by a competitive peer-review proposal award process as part of the user program. For purposes of reporting EMSL user data to DOE, EMSL tracks the number of active projects, active users by project, user institutions by project, as well as the number of distinct users and User institutions.

items.name: Enzyme nomenclature database
items.description: ENZYME is a repository of information relative to the nomenclature of enzymes. It is primarily based on the recommendations of the Nomenclature Committee of the International Union of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (IUBMB) and it describes each type of characterized enzyme for which an EC (Enzyme Commission) number has been provided. The database is complete and up to date. It is regularly updated to reflect updates and additions to the nomenclature.

items.name: EPA ChemView
items.description: EPA ChemView is a U.S. EPA database providing health and safety information on chemicals regulated under the amended Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA). It supports informed chemical safety decisions by offering public access to data submitted to or developed by the EPA under the Frank R. Lautenberg Chemical Safety Act.

items.name: Ersilia Model Hub
items.description: The Ersilia Model Hub is a unified open‑source platform offering pretrained AI/ML models for drug discovery in infectious and neglected diseases. You can run models online (no coding needed) or download them for local inference. It also enables contributions of models from literature or new custom models, promoting open access and reuse. As part of Ersilia’s mission, it empowers research in low‑resource settings by making AI/ML tools more accessible.

items.name: eSango
items.description:
CPUT eSango, a research data repository, powered by Figshare , is a multidisciplinary institutional research data repository that provides access to unique and scalable server architecture to facilitate data sharing, collaboration, storage, persistent archiving, and to showcase data from institutions to a large and growing community already used by other institutions and currently containing more than three million objects. The scope of the CPUT collection are from researchers and postgraduate students from CPUT's six faculties: Applied Sciences, Business and Management Sciences, Education, Engineering and the Built Environment, Health & Wellness Sciences, and Informatics and
Design.
licences: GNU Affero General Public License (AGPL) v3.0 only

items.name: ESS SciCat
items.description: Scicat is a metadata catalogue allows users to access information about experimental results, measured at the European Spallation Source (ESS).

items.name: EUDAT B2SHARE
items.description: B2SHARE is a repository for storing small-scale research data from diverse contexts. It guarantees long-term persistence of data (with permanent identifiers) and allows that data to be shared with other users. B2SHARE is integrated within the EUDAT collaborative data infrastructure. B2SHARE is open to all researchers and scientists who are affiliated with research institutions, universities as well as to individual researchers (citizen scientists).

items.name: European Chemical Biology Database
items.description: The European Chemical Biology Database (ECBD) collects experimental results from biological screening programs performed within the EU-OPENSCREEN platform. There are 3 chemical libraries in ECBD: bioactive, diverse, and academic. The bioactive library contains compounds selected with a strong emphasis on target coverage and selectivity. The diverse library contains compounds with unbiased chemical diversity, designed by five academic computational chemistry groups. In the academic library, compounds are collected from European chemists.

items.name: European Data Portal
items.description: The European Data Portal harvests the metadata of Public Sector Information available on public data portals across European countries. Information regarding the provision of data and the benefits of re-using data is also included.

items.name: Fairdata.fi
items.description: Fairdata services are part of the digital preservation services offered by the Ministry of Education and Culture, Finland (“Minedu”). The Fairdata services support the research process and management of digital data with some of the components described in the Framework for Open Science and Research.

items.name: FAIRDOMHub
items.description:
The FAIRDOMHub is a publicly available repository managed and supported by the FAIRDOM consortium (https://fair-dom.org/).
It's build using the FAIRDOM-SEEK software (http://fairdomseek.org), an open source web platform for storing, sharing and publishing research assets of biology projects. The assets include FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable) Data, Operating procedures and Models. 
FAIRDOMHub enables researchers to organize, share and publish data, models and protocols, interlink them in the context of the biology investigations that produced them, and to interrogate them via API interfaces. By using the FAIRDOMHub, researchers can achieve more effective exchange with geographically distributed collaborators during projects, ensure results are sustained and preserved and generate reproducible publications that adhere to the FAIR guiding principles of data stewardship. FAIRDOMHub includes special support for the Systems Biology community.

items.name: FDAT Research Data Repository
items.description: FDAT is the institutional research data repository of the University of Tübingen, designed for the long-term preservation, publication, and sharing of research data. It supports researchers from all scientific disciplines at the university and follows the FAIR data principles by providing standardized metadata, persistent DOIs, and open licensing options. The repository hosts a wide variety of datasets, software, and other research outputs, ensuring that they are discoverable, accessible, and reusable for the scientific community.

items.name: Federated Research Data Repository
items.description: The Federated Research Data Repository (FRDR) is a bilingual publishing platform for sharing and preserving Canadian research data. It is a curated, general-purpose repository, custom built for large datasets.

items.name: figshare
items.description: figshare is a generalist, subject-agnostic repository for many different types of digital objects that can be used without cost to researchers. Data can be submitted to the central figshare repository (described here), or institutional repositories using the figshare software can be installed locally, e.g. by universities and publishers. Metadata in figshare is licenced under is CC0. figshare has also partnered with DuraSpace and Chronopolis to offer further assurances that public data will be archived under the stewardship of Chronopolis. figshare is supported through Institutional, Funder, and Governmental service subscriptions.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: figshare Plus
items.description: Figshare Plus is a generalist, subject-agnostic repository created specifically to support large datasets (over 20GB, up to many TBs) and large files sizes.
