It is a repository where you can make any type of data or other output of your research publicly available and associate it with related publications and research projects. Figshare Plus offers data deposit as a one-time Data Publishing Charge (DPC) to share the datasets and materials supporting a specific publication or project.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication
Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-BY) v1.0

items.name: Flanders Research Information Space
items.description: FRIS (Flanders Research Information Space) is a regional research information portal that aggregates and provides up-to-date metadata on publicly funded research in Flanders, including researchers, projects, publications and other outputs. It aims to increase the visibility of Flemish research, support networking and interdisciplinary collaboration, and serve as a resource for reporting, analysis and policymaking.

items.name: FOUNDRY-ML
items.description: Foundry-ML is an open-source platform that provides curated, machine-learning-ready datasets for materials science and chemistry research. It offers structured datasets with standardized metadata, including tabular data, images, and hierarchical scientific data formats. The platform focuses on scientific data such as materials properties, chemical structures, experimental measurements, and simulation results to support reproducible ML workflows in scientific discovery.

items.name: Framework for Open and Reproducible Research Training - Replication Database
items.description: FORRT’s Replication Database (FReD) is a community-augmented, quantitative, meta-analytical interface of one of the most comprehensive collections of original and replication findings, including Replications and Reversals and large scale projects such as Many Labs or Registered Replication Reports. Via ReD, students, researchers, and applicants can create summaries of replication findings, search replications, investigate correlates of replicability, and automatically check for replications in reference lists.

items.name: FZ-Juelich B2SHARE
items.description: FZ-Juelich B2SHARE is a service developed by the EUDAT CDI. It provides researchers a solution for storing and sharing small-scale research data from diverse contexts. The local instance at Forschungszentrum Juelich is an offer for everyone within the research centre to share or publish their results with a URL and a PID (persistent identifier). B2SHARE can handle research data in a single file and distributed data across multiple files. The research data and additional metadata are stored in one record. While creating a record the user is able to fill in the (community specific) metadata. Each submitted record and each file within the record is provided with a PID. The PID can be used in publications to refer to the research data. The local B2SHARE instance at Forschungszentrum Juelich assigns DOIs as DataCite repository FZ-Juelich B2SHARE.

items.name: Galoá Proceedings.Science
items.description:
Proceedings.Science is an open access repository and publishing platform managed by Galoá. It is dedicated to hosting, organizing, and preserving conference proceedings, extended abstracts, and academic papers from various scientific events, ensuring they are findable and accessible to the global research community.

Galoá Science is a Crossref Sponsor and a member of the ORCID Consortia, ensuring persistent identifiers and interoperability for all hosted research objects.

items.name: Garden
items.description: Garden is a platform for publishing, discovering and running scientific AI models (in areas like materials science, structural biology and astrophysics). It provides each model as a runnable function with metadata, benchmarks and a consistent interface so researchers can quickly test or reuse models without dealing with intricate setup.

items.name: Geochemical Earth Reference Model
items.description: Geochemical Earth Reference Model contains summary data on the geochemistry of all reservoirs in the Earth. All search results are customizable, allowing the user to sort and convert units and to download the data in a format of your choice with one click. This relational database only includes peer-reviewed data.

items.name: Geochemistry of Rocks of the Oceans and Continents
items.description: The Geochemistry of Rocks of the Oceans and Continents (GEOROC) database is a collection of published analyses of igneous rocks and mantle xenoliths. It contains major and trace element concentrations, radiogenic and nonradiogenic isotope ratios as well as analytical ages for whole rocks, glasses, minerals and inclusions. Samples come from 11 different geological settings. Metadata include, among others, geographic location with latitude and longitude, rock class and rock type, alteration grade, analytical method, laboratory, reference materials and references.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: GeologyOntario
items.description: GeologyOntario is an online geoscience information portal maintained by the Government of Ontario that provides access to geological and mineral exploration information for the province. It contains geological maps, reports, assessment files, geophysical data, mineral and mining information, and other geoscience datasets. The platform brings together information compiled from government sources, historical records, and geoscience experts, with data and reports available for viewing and download. It is primarily used for geological research, mineral exploration, mining, and natural resource management.

items.name: Geothermal Data Repository
items.description: The GDR provides free access to data generated from projects funded by the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Geothermal Technologies Office.  It was established to receive, manage, and make available all geothermal-relevant data generated from DOE-funded projects.  Its primary objective is to make high-value data universally accessible and to to protect DOE’s investment in research and development through proper data management and the open transfer of knowledge, to fuel innovation, reduce duplication of effort, and promote scientific discovery in the geothermal sector.

items.name: GHDDI Info Sharing Portal
items.description: GHDDI Info Sharing Portal is the public information sharing portal and data repository for the drug discovery community, initiated by GHDDI. We are making our drug discovery capabilities and resources available at no cost to all researchers who are developing new treatments for COVID-19.

items.name: GitHub
items.description: GitHub Inc. is a Git-based software repository that provides version control. It offers all of the distributed version control and source code management (SCM) functionality of Git as well as adding its own features. It provides access control and several collaboration features such as bug tracking, feature requests, task management, and wikis for each project. It provides a number of different access levels, from free through to paid services.

items.name: GitLab
items.description: GitLab is a Git-based source code repository with wiki and issue tracker functionality. It provides a number of different access levels, from free through to a number of paid services.

items.name: Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking
items.description: Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking (GNPS) is a web-based mass spectrometry ecosystem that aims to be an open-access knowledge base for community-wide organization and sharing of raw, processed or identified tandem mass (MS/MS) spectrometry data. GNPS aids in identification and discovery throughout the entire life cycle of data; from initial data acquisition and analysis, to post publication exploration. GNPS provides the ability to analyze a data set and to compare it to all publicly available datasets by building on the computational infrastructure of the University of California San Diego (UCSD) Center for Computational Mass Spectrometry (CCMS), and providing public dataset deposition and/or retrieval through the Mass Spectrometry Interactive Virtual Environment (MassIVE) data repository. To provide open and transparent solutions for mass spectrometry (MS) data reuse, data sharing, and analysis reproducibility, the GNPS Dashboard collaborative interactive web application, provides tools to facilitate the exploration of liquid and gas chromatography(LC/GC)–mass spectrometry (MS) data for collaborative examination. The GNPS Dashboard is a hands-on platform for use of private and publicly available MS data, including files stored at long-term MS data repositories such as GNPS/MassIVE, MetaboLights, ProteomeXchange, and the Metabolomics Workbench.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: GlycoPOST
items.description: GlycoPOST is a mass spectrometry data repository for glycomics. Users can release their "raw/processed" data via this site with a unique identifier number for the paper publication. Submission conditions are in accordance with the Minimum Information Required for a Glycomics Experiment (MIRAGE) guidelines.

items.name: GlycoProtDB
items.description: GlycoProtDB is a glycoprotein database providing information of Asn (N)-glycosylated proteins and their glycosylated site(s), which were constructed by employing a bottom-up strategy using actual glycopeptide sequences identified by LC/MS-based glycoproteomic technologies. The database is searchable using gene ID, gene name, and its description (protein name) as query. Each data sheet of glycproteins is based on a single amino acid sequence in Wormpep database for C.elegans and NCBI Refseq database for mouse. The sheet presents actually detected N-glycosylation site(s) which are displayed each capturing methods of glycopeptide subset, e.g., lectins Concanavalin A, wheat germ agglutinin (WGA), or HILIC (hydrophilic interaction chromatography), as well as potential N-glycosylation sites (NX[STC], X≠P). Protein sequences, which have common glycopeptide sequence(s), are linked each other.

items.name: GlyCosmos Glycoscience Portal
items.description: The GlyCosmos Portal is a Web portal aiming to integrate the glycosciences with the life sciences. It consists of Standards, Repositories and Data Resources, providing information about genes, proteins, lipids, pathways and diseases.

items.name: GlyTouCan
items.description: The international glycan structure repository for glycans published in the literature. Any glycan structure, ranging in resolution from monosaccharide composition to fully defined structures can be registered and have an accession number assigned as long as there are no inconsistencies in the structure.

items.name: Griffith Research Online
items.description: Griffith Research Online is a digital archive of research and scholarship from Griffith University, Brisbane, Australia.

items.name: GRIIDC
items.description: GRIIDC is a multidisciplinary data repository that stores and disseminates data primarily collected or generated from the Gulf of Mexico region. Data can be searched and downloaded for free and data can be stored for a fee. Datasets are assigned digital object identifiers and are described with ISO-19115-2 metadata. Our mission is to ensure a data and information legacy that promotes continual scientific discovery and public awareness of coastal and marine ecosystems.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: GSA Data Repository
items.description: The GSA Data Repository was established in 1974 as an open archive in which authors of articles in GSA journals and books could place information that supplemented and/or expanded on their article. A unique number was included in a footnote with the printed article (ex: 2007001 is entry 1 for 2007). Hard copies were mailed on request until the Repository went online. In the early 2000s, the remaining hard copies were scanned and posted online as well. In 2020, GSA moved the Repository to Figshare.

items.name: Göttingen Research Online Data
items.description: Göttingen Research Online is an institutional repository for the publication of research data at the Göttingen Campus.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Harvard Dataverse Repository
items.description:
Harvard Dataverse Repository is a research data repository running on the open source Dataverse software. The repository is fully open to the public, allows upload and browsing of data from all fields of research, and is free for all researchers worldwide.

Harvard Dataverse Repository receives support from Harvard University, public and private grants, and an emergent consortium model.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication
Harvard Dataverse API Terms of Use
Harvard Dataverse General Terms of Use

items.name: heiDATA
items.description: heiDATA is Heidelberg University’s research data repository. It is managed by the Competence Centre for Research Data, a joint institution of the University Library and the Computing Centre. All researchers affiliated with Heidelberg University can use this service for archiving and publishing their data. heiDATA runs on software from the Dataverse Project.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: HELLANICUS Institutional Repository - University of the Aegean
items.description:
The Library HELLANICUS Institutional Repository of the University of the Aegean is a service for depositing digital documents which are produced by the Institution’s academic community as a result of its scientific and research activities and which, to a great extent, are not commercially available.

The main aim of the Hellanicus Institutional Repository is to collect, organize, publicize and maintain the scientific work of the members of the academic community in a way that ensures an easy and seamless access to it. Examples of this work include scientific articles - published or not - seminar lectures, textbooks, teaching material, dissertations and PhD theses, multimedia material and videotaped lectures.

items.name: Hellenic Academic Research Data Repository
items.description: HARDMIN (Hellenic Academic Research Data Management Initiative) is Greece’s national repository for research data produced by Greek researchers and academics. It provides secure storage, publication, and long-term access to research data, enhancing transparency, reusability, and digital transformation in the research field.

items.name: High Energy Physics Data Repository
items.description: The Durham High Energy Physics Database (HEPData) has been built up over the past four decades as a unique open-access repository for scattering data from experimental particle physics. It currently comprises the data points from plots and tables related to several thousand publications including those from the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). HEPData is funded by a grant from the UK STFC and is based at the IPPP at Durham University.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: HilReDa
items.description: HilReDa is the University of Hildesheim’s own research data repository. Members of the University of Hildesheim can publish their research results there in the form of research data. This ensures that the data is permanently preserved and made publicly available as open access in a sustainable and high-quality manner.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: IdeaExchange@UAkron
items.description: IdeaExchange@UAkron is the institutional repository for The University of Akron in the state of Ohio. A variety of research based documents and media are collected and preserved including working papers, published articles, conference proceedings, student theses, and archival materials. These documents are made available freely whenever possible.

items.name: IEEE DataPort™
items.description:
IEEE DataPort™ is an online data platform created, owned, and supported by IEEE, a technical professional organization. The web-based platform enables researchers to store, share, access and manage research data.
IEEE DataPort™ provides a DOI for each dataset, supports Open Access/Open Science initiatives, enables dataset owners to retain copyright and ownership rights, supplies data management workflows, and  and provides 2TB/dataset storage capacity for individuals and 10TB/dataset storage capacity for members of institutional subscribers.  All datasets are stored in Amazon AWS S3 to simplify dataset access, analysis and management. Standard datasets may be uploaded for free, and will then be available to DataPort™ subscribers. Data owners can also pay a fee to publish an "Open Access" dataset that is available to all IEEE DataPort™ users without requiring a paid subscription or membership. DataPort™ subscribers can also host private or public data competitions that provide non-subscribers with time-limited access to applicable dataset files.

items.name: IIT Dataverse
items.description: IIT Dataverse is the institutional research data repository of the Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia. IIT Dataverse has been operative since May 2021 and is currently open to IIT-affiliated researchers for research data deposition and sharing.

items.name: Illinois Data Bank
items.description: The Illinois Data Bank is a public access repository for publishing research data from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

items.name: Imperial College Research Computing Service Data Repository
items.description: A lightweight digital repository for data based on the concepts of collections of filesets and the relationships between them. Both the collection and the fileset are assigned a DOI by the DataCite organisation which can be quoted in articles. Browsing and data deposition are available only when logged in.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: INCLUDE Data Hub
items.description: The INCLUDE (INvestigation of Co-occurring conditions across the Lifespan to Understand Down syndromE) Project is an NIH-wide collaboration that seeks to improve health and quality-of-life for people with Down syndrome. The INCLUDE Project Data Coordinating Center and partners created the INCLUDE Data Hub, a centralized data resource that allows access to large-scale clinical and multi-omics datasets specific to Down syndrome and supports collaborative, cloud-based analysis to accelerate scientific discoveries related to Down syndrome and its co-occurring conditions.

items.name: India Data Portal
items.description: India Data Portal 2.0 emerges as the country's first research initiative dedicated to public service, offering geo-coded, LGD-mapped, high-spatial time series data from government sources, integrating technological innovation to establish data as a public good.

items.name: Information Platform for Chemical Monitoring
items.description: IPCHEM - the Information Platform for Chemical Monitoring is the reference access point for discovering chemical monitoring data collections which are managed by and are available to European Commission bodies, Member States, international and national organisations and research communities.

items.name: Infoscience - EPFL Institutional Repository
items.description: Infoscience is the institutional repository of EPFL for disseminating scientific publications and research output. It collects, preserves and shares the academic and scientific output of EPFL researchers, teachers and students, making it freely accessible to the largest possible audience.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: INFRA-ART Spectral Library
items.description: The INFRA-ART Spectral Library is a FAIR data service designed as a digital support tool for heritage research specialists working with spectroscopic techniques. With over 3,000 curated spectra, the database allows users to analyze and compare the spectral signatures of a wide range of reference materials, facilitating the identification of 'unknown' samples. The INFRA-ART Spectral Library has been designed, implemented, and optimized over several years, and it currently integrates ATR-FTIR, XRF, Raman, and SWIR reflectance spectra on over 1,400 different materials typically found in works of art.

items.name: Institut Laue-Langevin Data Portal
items.description: The Institut Laue-Langevin (ILL) Data Portal is a repository for storage and access to experimental data obtained at the ILL. While individual DOIs for data are accessible, full access to the database, including searching and browsing, requires a login.

items.name: Integrated Public Use Microdata Series - International
items.description: IPUMS-International is an effort to inventory, preserve, harmonize, and disseminate census microdata from around the world. The data are coded and documented consistently across countries and over time to facilitate comparative research. IPUMS-International makes these data available to qualified researchers free of charge through a web dissemination system.

items.name: International Ocean Discovery Program Laboratory Information Management System
items.description: The International Ocean Discovery Program (IODP) is an international research collaboration that coordinates seagoing expeditions to study the history of the Earth recorded in sediments and rocks beneath the ocean floor. This resource contains Phase II of the Integrated Ocean Drilling Program and all of the International Ocean Discovery Program data in the new system.

items.name: Internet Archive
items.description: The Internet Archive, a 501(c)(3) non-profit, is building a digital library of Internet sites and other cultural artifacts in digital form. Like a paper library, we provide free access to researchers, historians, scholars, people with print disabilities, and the general public. Our mission is to provide Universal Access to All Knowledge.

items.name: ioChem-BD
items.description: ioChem-BD is a digital repository of Computational Chemistry and Materials results. A set of modules and tools aimed to manage large volumes of quantum chemistry results from a wide variety of broadly used simulation packages.
licences: GNU Affero General Public License (AGPL) v3.0 only

items.name: Iowa Research Online - University of Iowa Repository
items.description: Iowa Research Online (ISSN 2476-1680 (online)) preserves and provides access to the research and creative scholarship created by the University of Iowa's faculty, students, and staff. The research papers, theses, dissertations, books, conference presentations, journals, data and multimedia here represent Iowa's rich intellectual and cultural community.

items.name: Iowa State University's DataShare
items.description: Iowa State University’s DataShare is an open access repository for sharing, publishing, and archiving research data created by Iowa State University scholars and researchers.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication
ISU Data Share Terms of Use

items.name: ISIS DataGateway
items.description: The ISIS DataGateway is a web-based data repository and discovery portal for the ISIS Neutron and Muon Source (UK) that allows users to browse, explore and visualise experimental data from large-scale science facilities. It supports long-term archival, ingestion and metadata indexing of data to enable better accessibility, reuse and citation of scientific datasets.

items.name: IsoArcH database
items.description: IsoArcH is a non-profit initiative dedicated to preserving and sharing isotopic data for research worldwide.

items.name: ISTA Research Explorer
items.description: ISTA Research Explorer (ISTA REx) is the institutional repository of the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA), showcasing the institute's scholarly output. It provides long-term access to publications, research data, software, theses, conference papers, and technical reports, assigning DOIs to eligible research outputs. The repository supports open science by enabling researchers to share, preserve, and link their research outputs while complying with institutional and funder open access requirements.

items.name: IZTECH GCRIS Premium Database
items.description: GCRIS is an institutional research information system and open academic repository run by the Izmir Institute of Technology.

items.name: Johns Hopkins Research Data Repository
items.description: The Johns Hopkins Research Data Repository is an open-access institutional platform designed to collect, preserve, and share research data produced by Johns Hopkins University researchers. It hosts datasets from a broad range of disciplines, including medicine, public health, engineering, natural sciences, and social sciences. The repository contains materials such as experimental data, survey datasets, computational outputs, and accompanying documentation or code. Its purpose is to support transparency, reproducibility, and long-term access to research data.

items.name: Kaggle Datasets
items.description: Kaggle Datasets is a public open data platform which combines data, users, discussions, and software. Datasets can be searched, bookmarked and explored via Kernels and discussions. All types of data are allowed. Individual users and organizations can register. Datasets can be published either privately or shared publicly.

items.name: Karnataka Open Data Portal
items.description: Open Government Data Portal of Karnataka is a platform for supporting Open Data initiative of Government of Karnataka. The portal is intended to be used by Departments/Organizations of Government of Karnataka to publish datasets, documents, services, tools and applications collected by them for public use. It intends to increase transparency in the functioning of the state Government and also open avenues for many more innovative uses of Government Data to give different perspective.

items.name: Karolinska Institutet Data Repository
items.description: KI Data Repository is the institutional data repository for Karolinska Institutet (KI). KI Data Repository accepts data where KI is the research principle, i.e. where KI is the organization responsible for the data. KI Data Repository’s mission is to curate, preserve, and provide continued access to KI’s research data.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Khazar University Institutional Repository
items.description: Khazar University Institutional Repository (KUIR) is the open access digital archive of scholarly research produced by the faculty, students, and collaborators of Khazar University in Baku, Azerbaijan.

items.name: Kidney Tissue Atlas
items.description: The Kidney Tissue Atlas is a part of the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), Kidney Precision Medicine Project (KPMP) initiative in part of a multi-site collaboration comprised of patients, clinicians, and investigators from across the United States. The Atlas Repository provides access to the datasets being generated by KPMP. The datasets available in the repository are a combination of raw and processed data from KPMP participant biopsies and reference tissue samples. Datasets are routinely added as they are generated and QCed prior to release.

items.name: KiltHub
items.description: KiltHub is a comprehensive institutional repository, maintained by the Carnegie Mellon University Libraries and hosted on the figshare platform, where CMU researchers and their collaborators can share the scholarly outputs and research data produced in the course of their research. KiltHub curates, collects, preserves, and provides open access to this material as part of the Libraries' commitment to open scholarship and collaboration.

items.name: Kinetic Database for Astrochemistry
items.description: KIDA (KInetic Database for Astrochemistry) is a database of kinetic data of interest for astrochemical (interstellar medium and planetary atmospheres) studies. KIDA is a project initiated by different communities in order to 1) improve the interaction between astrochemists and physico-chemists and 2) simplify the work of modeling the chemistry of astrophysical environments. Here astrophysical environments stand for the interstellar medium and planetary atmospheres. Both types of environments use similar chemical networks and the physico-chemists who work on the determination of reaction rate coefficients for both types of environment are the same.

items.name: Kitchener GeoHub
items.description: The Open Kitchener GIS database is the City of Kitchener’s open data portal hosted on ArcGIS Hub. It provides free public access to a wide range of geospatial and municipal datasets that anyone can download or use in apps, maps, and analyses.

items.name: Knowledge Base of the University of Gdańsk
items.description: The Knowledge Base of the University of Gdańsk is a system for collecting the scientific achievements of employees, doctoral students, and students of the University of Gdańsk. It also serves as the institutional repository of the University of Gdańsk. The Knowledge Base repository complies with the 5-star Open Data and FAIR Data principles, integrates with DataCite, and is indexed by OpenAIRE. The repository can store and share research data from all scientific disciplines. Research data can be deposited either in an open-access model or in restricted access, visible only to logged-in users of the Knowledge Base. Functional capabilities of the Knowledge Base repository are: assigning permanent, unique DOI identifiers; versioning and dataset verification by data stewards.

items.name: Knowledge Network for Biocomplexity
items.description: The Knowledge Network for Biocomplexity (KNB) is an international repository intended to facilitate ecological and environmental research. KNB was created to share, discover, access and interpret complex ecological data. Contextual information provided with KNB data allows scientists to integrate and analyze data. The data originate from a highly-distributed set of field stations, laboratories, research sites, and individual researchers. The foundation of the KNB is the detailed metadata provided by researchers, which promotes both automated and manual integration of data into new projects. As part of the KNB effort, data management software is developed in a free and open source manner, so other groups can build upon the tools. The KNB is powered by the Metacat data management system, and is optimized for handling data sets described using the Ecological Metadata Language, but can store any XML-based metadata document.

items.name: Knowledge Repository of the Central University of Punjab Library
items.description: Knowledge Repository is a service initiated by the Central University of Punjab Library that provides long-term access to the scholarly resources generated by the University. The primary objective of this service is to collect, organize, preserve and provide access and dissemination of scholarly resources produced by the faculty members, student, staff and other members of the University Community. Submissions include (but are not limited to) journal articles, conference papers, book chapters, working papers, report, theses and dissertations.

items.name: KonDATA
items.description: KonDATA is the research data repository of the University of Konstanz. This service offered by KIM provides members of the University of Konstanz with the simple and convenient option of publishing research data in a way that is FAIR, visible and citable in the long term.

items.name: KU Leuven RDR
items.description: RDR (pronounced 'Radar') is the curated institutional research data repository of KU Leuven. The repository contains published data resulting from KU Leuven research in a FAIR way and allows the published data to be as open as possible, but as closed as necessary. The institutional repository helps KU Leuven researchers publish, share, cite, and preserve their research data in a findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable way, with support from university staff. The repository uses the open source Dataverse project software as its base.
licences: GNU Affero General Public License (AGPL) v3.0 only

items.name: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes
items.description: KEGG is a database resource for understanding high-level functions and utilities of the biological system, such as the cell, the organism and the ecosystem, from molecular-level information, especially large-scale molecular datasets generated by genome sequencing and other high-throughput experimental technologies.

items.name: Lancashire Online Research Data
items.description: Lancashire Online Research Data enables researchers at the University of Lancashire to store, manage and share research data securely, ensuring it can be discovered and accessed where appropriate. The repository enhances the visibility and integrity of the University's research, supports the responsible reuse of high-quality data, and promotes collaboration, knowledge exchange, and public engagement.

items.name: Lancaster University Institutional Data Repository
items.description:
Lancaster University's Institutional Data Repository contains datasets published internally by researchers at Lancaster University. It also contains a partial registry of externally published datasets by dataset creators affiliated with the institution. 

Datasets are available in 3 methods of access: 
1. Open 
2. Restricted where data is available on request to rdm@lancaster.ac.uk
3. Closed or Metadata records only
licences: Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODC ODbL) v1.0

items.name: Land Portal
items.description: The Land Portal Foundation was established to create, curate and disseminate land governance information by fostering an inclusive and accessible data landscape. The Land Portal aims to improve the documentation, mapping, and monitoring of land governance issues, democratize access to land data across all levels, and promote informed global dialogue on land-related challenges.

items.name: Launchpad
items.description: Launchpad is a software and source code repository with a number of features including bug tracking, translations, new feature tracking and both Bazaar and Git version control.

items.name: Leeds Beckett University - Thesis and Research Data Repository
items.abbreviation: Leeds Beckett Thesis and Research Data Repository
items.description:
Leeds Beckett University's Thesis and Research Data Repository (Figshare) enables theses and archived data to be made Open Access. Our outputs are protected under a Creative Commons licence. 
Theses and research data are available to download from the Repository, which can be found through search engines and accessed by anyone, increasing the views and potential impact of the research. Each record has a DOI enabling easy sharing.

items.name: Leibniz Data Manager
items.description: The Leibniz Data Manager (LDM) is an open research data repository and management system hosted by the Technische Informationsbibliothek (TIB) that helps researchers publish, search, and explore scientific datasets across disciplines.

items.name: Library Open Access Repository
items.description: The LOAR (Library Open Access Repository) is an open data repository established in 2016 for Danish research data. It is run by the Royal Danish Library and aims to provide open access data, help researchers meet Danish and European grant requirements, and enable data reuse where appropriate.

items.name: Liverpool John Moores University Data Repository
items.description: LJMU open repositories allow LJMU researchers depositing their publications and data to make them accessible to a wider audience and comply with funder and institutional requirements.

items.name: London Datastore
items.description: The London Datastore is a free and open data-sharing portal where anyone can access data relating to the capital. Whether you’re a citizen, business owner, researcher or developer, the site provides over a thousand datasets to help you understand the city and develop solutions to London’s problems.

items.name: Loughborough Research Repository
items.description: The Loughborough Research Repository is an open-access digital archive that collects and preserves the research outputs of Loughborough University. It provides access to a wide range of scholarly materials, including journal articles, conference papers, doctoral theses, and research datasets. The repository aims to increase the visibility, accessibility, and long-term preservation of the university’s research.

items.name: Lunaris
items.description: Lunaris is Canada’s national discovery service for multidisciplinary data from research institutions across the country. Datasets from over 90 academic, government, and research repositories are made discoverable in a bilingual interface that provides keyword and map-based searching.

items.name: MacEwan University Data Repository
items.description: The MacEwan University Data Repository provides a place to store, share, and explore data that supports the teaching and scholarly activity of MacEwan University.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Macquarie University Research Data Repository
items.description: The Macquarie University Research Data Repository (RDR) is an institutional platform where Macquarie University researchers can publish, showcase and share research data.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Macromolecular Xtallography Raw Data Repository
items.description: MX-RDR (Macromolecular Crystallography Raw Data Repository) is an open-access scientific database designed to archive and share raw diffraction data from macromolecular crystallography experiments. It stores datasets related to crystal structure studies along with rich metadata extracted from images, user input, and Protein Data Bank deposits. The platform allows users to search, access, and download data freely to support reuse and reproducibility in structural biology research.

items.name: MADATA - Mannheim Research Data Repository
items.description: MADATA is the research data repository of the University of Mannheim where university researchers can archive and share diverse research data. It stores a wide range of digital research outputs including, datasets, code, documentation, and other materials that support scientific studies in fields like social sciences, computer science, natural sciences, and beyond.

items.name: mapMECFS
items.description: mapMECFS houses Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) research data and results from across many biological and clinical disciplines. This interactive data portal enables exploration and access to complex experimental data with the goal of advancing ME/CFS discoveries, including diagnosis and treatments. Data types shared on mapMECFS include, but are not limited to, metabolomics, gene expression, microbiome, demographic, health and survey data, and others.

items.name: Markham Open Data Portal
items.description: The Markham Open Data Portal is a free and open data-sharing portal providing access to the definitive source of geographic and other data relating to the City of Markham.
licences: Open Data Licence - City of Markham

items.name: Mass Spectrometry Interactive Virtual Environment
items.description: MassIVE is a worldwide mass spectrometry data repository integrated into a flexible, scalable, user-friendly framework offering a diverse set of data analysis algorithms and tools. MassIVE is a  mass spectrometry community resource data repository, developed the Center for Computational Mass Spectrometry (CCMS), designed to store, browse, redistribute, re-analyze and integrate all publicly available mass spectrometry data in promoting globally accessible and free exchange of mass spectrometry data. The MassIVE data repository provides reliable sharing of primary data in addition to offering user-friendly tools for advanced data analysis and visualization.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: MassBank of North America
items.description: MassBank of North America (MoNA) is a repository of mass spectral data for small molecules and other compounds. It provides experimental and computationally generated mass spectra together with compound identifiers, chemical structures, and associated metadata. The database supports compound identification and spectral matching in metabolomics, mass spectrometry, analytical chemistry, and related fields.

items.name: Materials Cloud
items.description: The Materials Cloud Archive provides FAIR & long-term storage of research data from computational materials science, with particular focus on sharing the full provenance of calculations.

items.name: mediaTUM
items.description: mediaTUM is the institutional open access repository of the Technical University of Munich (TUM), used to publish and archive digital academic content such as theses, research data, articles, images and multimedia collections. It supports researchers and students in managing, publishing and discovering scientific publications and research outputs.

items.name: Mendeley Data
items.description: Mendeley Data is a multidisciplinary, free-to-use open repository specialised for research data. Files of any format can be uploaded and shared with the research community following the FAIR data principles, up to a maximum of 10GB per dataset. Each version of a dataset is given a unique DOI, and dark archived with DANS (Data Archiving and Networking Services), ensuring that every dataset and citation will be valid in perpetuity. Datasets can be licensed under a range of open licences, and datasets are and will continue to be free access. Mendeley Data supports embargoing of data both generally and while undergoing peer review. It is funded by a subscription model for Academic & Government entities.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: MetaboBank
items.description: MetaboBank is a public repository for metabolomics data obtained from mass spectrometry (MS), NMR, and imaging MS. Metadata are described in the MAGE-TAB format, which is standard in functional genomics and proteomics.
licences: International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration Policy

items.name: Metabolic Atlas
items.description: Metabolic Atlas is a web platform integrating open-source genome scale metabolic models (GEMs) for easy browsing and analysis. The goal is to collect curated GEMs, and to bring these models closer to FAIR principles. The website provides visualisations and comparisons of the GEMs, and links to resources, algorithms, other databases, and more general software applications. Metabolic Atlas is intended to be used for applications in metabolomics, clinical chemistry, biomarker discovery and general education. In short, the vision is to create a one-stop-shop for everything metabolism related.

items.name: MetaboLights
items.description: MetaboLights is a database for metabolomics studies, their raw experimental data and associated metadata. The database is cross-species and cross-technique and it covers metabolite structures and their reference spectra as well as their biological roles and locations. MetaboLights is the recommended metabolomics repository for a number of leading journals and ELIXIR, the European infrastructure for life science information.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Metabolomics Workbench
items.description: The Metabolomics Workbench serves as a national and international repository for metabolomics data and metadata and provides analysis tools and access to metabolite standards, protocols, tutorials, training, and more.
licences: NIH Common Fund Metabolomics Data Sharing Plan

items.name: Metabolonote
items.description: Metabolonote is a specialized database system that manages metadata for experimental data obtained through the study of Metabolomics. This system was developed with the aim of promoting the publication and utilization of Metabolomics data by simplifying the metadata recording process.

items.name: METASPACE
items.description: The METASPACE platform hosts an engine for metabolite annotation of imaging mass spectrometry data as well as a spatial metabolite knowledgebase of the metabolites from thousands of public datasets provided by the community. The METASPACE engine open online platform provides tools for integrated into validated workflows for clinical use exploratory analysis. Submit or interact with high-resolution imaging mass spectrometry (HR imaging MS) spatial data, explore knowledgeable annotations from all datasets using the interactive interface, collaborate with project team members on dataset annotation, or export the metabolite annotations to mine hundreds of thousands of metabolites found in community-provided datasets.

items.name: MIDAS
items.description: MIDAS is Lithuania’s National Open Access Research Data Archive, managed by Vilnius University, for storing, managing, publishing and discovering research data across all disciplines.

items.name: Middlesex University Research Data Repository
items.description: The Middlesex University Research Data Repository provides wide access to any openly-available digital content online.

items.name: Missouri University of Science and Technology Scholars' Mine
items.description: Scholars' Mine is an online collection of scholarly and creative works produced by the faculty, staff, and students of the Missouri University of Science and Technology. This digital repository is a service of Missouri S&T Library and Learning Resources.

items.name: Molecular Glue and Ternary binding database
items.description: MGTbind database contains 3,093 manually curated MGs with their chemical structures and physicochemical properties, along with 3,924 ternary interactions with bioactivity measurements (e.g. degradation capacities for MG degraders, in vitro biochemical activities and cellular activities). Hierarchical binding affinity is also collected to enable exploring of cooperative binding mechanisms. Ternary complex structural data are systematically integrated, either from the Protein Data Bank or generated by AlphaFold 3. All of them can be intuitively analyzed and visualized along with various predicted metrics. A fully functional and user-friendly web interface that allows global search and smooth browsing is provided and is freely accessible at https://mgtbind.pkumdl.cn.

items.name: Multi-Omics Research Factory
items.description: MORF (Multi-Omics Research Factory) was initially created by the BBSRC-funded DETOX project, led by Prof. Gavin Thomas at the University of York, to manage large and complex multi-omics datasets. Built by biologists for biologists, it allows the whole team to access the data securely from their browser, without the need for programming skills. As data becomes publicly available, it can be accessed and further analysed here. MORF's tools are also freely-available and include the MORF genome browser, which incorporates over 100 microbial genomes, and MORFlux, a flux balance analysis (FBA) modelling tool.

items.name: mzCloud
items.description: mzCloud is a web-based mass spectral database designed to support the identification of small molecules using tandem mass spectrometry. It contains an extensively curated collection of high-quality MSⁿ spectra organized into searchable spectral trees, along with compound structures, fragments, and related metadata. Researchers can search the database to match experimental spectra and aid in compound identification, and registered users can build custom spectral libraries.

items.name: NanoCommons Knowledge Base
items.description: The NanoCommons Knowledge Base is a data source provided by the NanoCommons project. It is based on the BioXM TM Knowledge Management Environment, developed over the last 15 years by Biomax Informatics AG and applied in multiple collaborative research projects and commercial environments. This database requires registration. NanoCommons provides a community framework and infrastructure for reproducible science and in-silico workflows for nanomaterials safety assessment

items.name: nanoHUB Results Database
items.description:
nanoHUB supports the deployment and publication of various types of tools and Apps. These include Apps created using Rappture or Sim2Ls. Results from successful runs are automatically indexed and
stored in a globally accessible database, the ResultsDB.

items.name: NASA Ames PAH IR Spectroscopic Database
items.description: Collaboration between the astronomers, laboratory chemists and theoretical chemists at the facilities of NASA's Ames Research Center resulted in the collection of PAH spectra known as The NASA Ames PAH IR Spectroscopic Database. Collaboration with different institutes, across several countries, helped mature the database and allowed for the construction of the web-portal with its data and tools. Initially intended for astronomers to explain the astronomical unidentified infrared bands and to investigate the "PAH hypothesis", now the spectral data and developed paradigms prove also valuable to, e.g., chemists, environmentalists, pharmacologists and nano-technologists.
licences: The Astrophysics & Astrochemistry Laboratory's Terms of Service

items.name: NASA GeneLab
items.description: NASA GeneLab expands scientists’ access to experiments that explore the molecular response of terrestrial biology to spaceflight environments. The vast amounts of raw data generated by experiments aboard the International Space Station are being made available to a worldwide community of scientists and computational researchers.

items.name: National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON)
items.description: The National Science Foundation's National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) is a continental-scale observation facility research data infrastructure, operated by Battelle, and designed to collect long-term open access ecological data. The NEON data portal provides access to standardized and quality-controlled data product types including meteorological, soil, organismal, biogeochemical, freshwater aquatic, and remote sensing data across application domains.

items.name: National Geothermal Data System
items.description: The National Geothermal Data System (NGDS) is a distributed data portal that provides access to geothermal energy–related datasets and metadata from multiple providers, including government agencies, research institutions, and industry partners. It allows users to search, visualize, and download geoscientific information such as well data, geochemistry, heat flow, and geothermal resource maps through a centralized web interface.

items.name: National Metadata Directory
items.description: The National Metadata Directory (NMD) is a central aggregator of metadata for scientific datasets in the Czech Republic. The NMD collects metadata from all repositories within the National Repository Platform and from other repositories containing datasets created by the Czech academic community. It serves as the primary discovery point across repositories and directs users to the primary repositories where the datasets reside.

items.name: National Omics Data Encyclopedia
items.description:
NODE (The National Omics Data Encyclopedia) provides an integrated, compatible, comparable, and scalable multi-omics resource platform that supports flexible data management and effective data release.  NODE uses a hierarchical data architecture to support storage of muti-omics data including sequencing data, MS based proteomics data, MS or NMR based metabolomics data, and fluorescence imaging data.
Launched in early 2017, NODE has collected and published over 900 terabytes of omics data for researchers from China and all over the world in last three years, 22% of which contains multiple omics data. NODE provides functions around the whole life cycle of omics data, from data archive, data requests/responses to data sharing, data analysis, data review and publish.
licences: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 China Mainland  (CC BY 3.0 CN)

items.name: National repository of academic texts
items.description:
The National Repository is a nationwide distributed electronic database in which academic texts are accumulated, stored and systemized. Academic text is a work of a scientific, scientific and technical, educational nature. The purpose of the National Repository is to make the scientific information as accessible to the public as possible for Ukraine and the world, which will contribute to the development of educational, scientific, scientific and technical, innovative activities by improving access to academic texts and promoting academic integrity.

The following types of academic texts in electronic form should be included in the NRAT: dissertations for the scientific degrees and abstracts of dissertations; qualification graduation work of higher education applicants; articles in scientific publications, including all articles (set of articles) on the basis of protection of which the degree has been awarded; monographs, including those for which a scientific degree has been awarded; scientific publications; reports on scientific, scientific and technical activities; deposited scientific works; textbooks, tutorials and other scientific, scientific and teaching materials; publications published by authors on online platforms for the exchange of scientific publications.

The National Repository consists of a central repository maintained by the National Repository Manager, and local repositories maintained by institutional participants.

The National Repository includes all academic texts, regardless of the date of their creation and promulgation in accordance with the established procedure in Regulation.

The National Repository Manager establishes a register of academic texts that is open and contains bibliographic information about academic texts that are included in the central and local repositories, as well as published in electronic or paper forms.

items.name: National Science Digital Library
items.description: The National Science Digital Library provides high quality online educational resources for teaching and learning, with current emphasis on the sciences, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) disciplines—both formal and informal, institutional and individual, in local, state, national, and international educational settings. The NSDL collection contains structured descriptive information (metadata) about web-based educational resources held on other sites by their providers. These providers have contribute this metadata to NSDL for organized search and open access to educational resources via this website and its services.

items.name: Natural History Museum Data Portal
items.description: The British natural history collection is one of the most important in the world, documenting 4.5 billion years of life, the Earth and the solar system. Almost all animal, plant, mineral and fossil groups are represented. The portal's main dataset consists of specimens from the Museum's collection database, with over 4 million records from the Museum’s Palaeontology, Mineralogy, Botany, Entomology and Zoology collections.
licences: Natural History Museum Data Portal Terms and conditions

items.name: Natural Products Magnetic Resonance Database
items.description: The Natural Products Magnetic Resonance Database is a freely available cloud-based, user-friendly, FAIR electronic database. NP-MRD accepts NMR data and associated metadata from newly undertaken NP studies. The NP-MRD accepts raw (time domain data, processed spectra, assigned chemical shifts, J-couplings, RDCs, etc.), and meta-data (structures, sources, methods, taxonomy, geospatial data, etc) from natural products ranging from purified substances to crude extracts, in all major solvents. The NP-MRD includes NPs such as vitamins, minerals, and probiotics as well as small molecules derived from plants, fungi, bacteria, marine organisms, or animals.

items.name: NCI Data Catalogue
items.description: The NCI Data Catalogue (https://geonetwork.nci.org.au/) is the discovery portal for the research collections, datasets and data services hosted at the National Computational Infrastructure (NCI Australia). It provides a searchable interface for NCI Australia's growing collection of datasets across a range of research disciplines.

items.name: NERC British Oceanographic Data Centre Data Archive
items.description: BODC makes available biological, chemical, physical and geophysical data on the marine environment.

items.name: Network Repository
items.description: The first interactive data and network data repository with real-time visual analytics. Network repository is not only the first interactive repository, but also the largest network repository with thousands of donations in 30+ domains (from biological to social network data). This large comprehensive collection of network graph data is useful for making significant research findings as well as benchmark network data sets for a wide variety of applications and domains (e.g., network science, bioinformatics, machine learning, data mining, physics, and social science) and includes relational, attributed, heterogeneous, streaming, spatial, and time series network data as well as non-relational machine learning data. All graph data sets are easily downloaded into a standard consistent format. We also have built a multi-level interactive graph analytics engine that allows users to visualize the structure of the network data as well as macro-level graph data statistics as well as important micro-level network properties of the nodes and edges.

items.name: NIE Data Repository
items.description: NIE Data Repository is the institutional research data repository for National Institute of Education (NIE), Singapore. The Repository is open to NIE researchers and staff to archive, publish and share their final research data related to publications.

items.name: NIH Human BioMolecular Atlas Program Data Portal
items.description: The HuBMAP Data Portal is the central resource for discovery, visualization, and download of single-cell tissue data generated by the Human BioMolecular Atlas Program consortium. HuBMAP tools and maps are openly available, inclusice of a standardized data curation and processing workflow ensure that only high quality is released. The HuBMAP Data Portal aims to be an open map of the human body at the cellular level to accelerate efforts to understand the relationships between the organization of cells and tissues, biological function, and human health from fresh, fixed, or frozen healthy human tissue using in situ and dissociative techniques that have high-spatial resolution data.

items.name: NIRD Research Data Archive
items.description: The NIRD Research Data Archive (RDA) is a long-term storage service for research data developed by Sigma2/NRIS that supports Open Science by allowing researchers to upload and manage datasets of any size or field.

items.name: NIST Science Data Portal
items.description: This National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Science Data Portal provides a user-friendly discovery and exploration tool for publicly available datasets at NIST. These data products are generated as part of the NIST mission, spanning multiple disciplines of scientific, engineering and technology research. NIST's publicly available data sets showcase its commitment to providing accurate, well-curated measurements of physical properties, exemplified by the Standard Reference Data program , as well as its commitment to advancing basic research.

items.name: nmrshiftdb2
items.description: nmrshiftdb2 is an NMR database for organic structures and their nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra. It allows for spectrum prediction (13C, 1H and other nuclei) as well as for searching spectra, structures and other properties. It also features peer-reviewed submission of datasets by its users. The nmrshiftdb2 software is open source, the data is published under an open content license.

items.name: nmrXiv
items.description: nmrXiv (pronounced nm-archive) is a FAIR and Open, Consensus-Driven Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) Data Repository and Computational platform. It is currently being developed as a part of the NFDI4Chem initiative with the ultimate goal of accelerating broader coordination and data sharing among researchers by creating a platform for managing, sharing, and analyzing raw and processed NMR spectral data.
licences: Community Data License Agreement - Permissive, v1.0 (CDLA-Permissive-1.0)
Community Data License Agreement - Sharing, v1.0.
Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication
Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication & License (PDDL) v1.0

items.name: NOMAD
items.description: NOMAD is a free web service that allows you to share your data or use comprehensive data provided by others. You can use NOMAD to organize, analyze, share, and publish your materials science data, as well as explore, download, and analyze the data of your colleagues. NOMAD is not only about sharing files, it is about sharing data and making data FAIR. All data in NOMAD are organized in well-defined structures described by a formal schema.

items.name: NORMAN Digital Sample Freezing Platform
items.description: The NORMAN Digital Sample Freezing Platform (DSFP) is a European infrastructure developed by the NORMAN Network to archive and share high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) data. It was developed by the NORMAN Network and includes functionalities for the application of retrospective suspect screening of thousands of contaminants of emerging concern.
licences: Creative Commons Attribution Share Alike 3.0 Austria (CC-BY-SA 3.0 AT)

items.name: NORMAN Substance Database
items.description: NORMAN SusDat is a compilation of information provided by NORMAN network members and has merged many chemical lists provided to the NORMAN Suspect List Exchange (NORMAN-SLE) into a common format and includes selected identifiers and predicted values as a service for NORMAN members. NORMAN-SLE, established in 2015 as a central access point for NORMAN members (and others) to find suspect lists relevant for their environmental monitoring question, is a part of this resource.

items.name: Nottingham Research Data Management Repository
items.description: The Nottingham Research Data Management Repository is the University of Nottingham’s institutional platform for storing, publishing, and sharing multidisciplinary research datasets produced by its researchers.

items.name: Nova Scotia Government's Open Data Portal
items.description: The Nova Scotia Open Data Portal is an open government data repository that provides free access to datasets published by the Government of Nova Scotia. It contains data, maps, charts, and other resources covering topics such as social services, the economy, government administration, transportation, and the environment. The portal was launched in 2016 to improve government transparency, encourage innovation, and support research, business, and public use of government data.

items.name: NSF Arctic Data Center
items.description: The Arctic Data Center is the primary data and software repository for the Arctic section of NSF Polar Programs. The Center helps the research community to reproducibly preserve and discover all products of NSF-funded research in the Arctic, including data, metadata, software, documents, and provenance that links these together. The repository is open to contributions from NSF Arctic investigators, and data are released under an open license (CC-BY, CC0, depending on the choice of the contributor). All science, engineering, and education research supported by the NSF Arctic research program are included, such as Natural Sciences (Geoscience, Earth Science, Oceanography, Ecology, Atmospheric Science, Biology, etc.) and Social Sciences (Archeology, Anthropology, Social Science, etc.).
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: NYCU Dataverse
items.description: The NYCU Dataverse is the institutional research data repository of National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University (NYCU), Taiwan, established to preserve, share, and promote the reuse of the university's research data. It enables NYCU researchers to publish finalized datasets with persistent identifiers (DOIs), making them citable, discoverable, and accessible to the global research community. The repository supports open science by facilitating long-term preservation, data sharing, and compliance with funder and journal data-sharing requirements.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: OEDataRep INGV - Osservatorio Etneo Open Data repository
items.description: Open Data repository focused on dataset publication by INGV OE - Osservatorio Etneo. The Catania-Osservatorio Etneo Section is a public scientific institution of the National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology (INGV) which carries out research, monitoring and surveillance activities in the fields of geophysics and volcanology.

items.name: Omics Discovery Index
items.description: The Omics Discovery Index (OmicsDI) provides dataset discovery across a heterogeneous, distributed group of Transcriptomics, Genomics, Proteomics and Metabolomics data resources, including both open and controlled access data resources. The resource provides a short description of every dataset, including accession, description, sample/data protocols biological evidences, and publication. Based on these metadata, OmicsDI provides extensive search capabilities, as well as identification of related datasets by metadata and data content where possible. In particular, OmicsDI identifies groups of related, multi-omics datasets across repositories by shared identifiers.

items.name: OmicsPred
items.description: OmicsPred is a resource for predicting multi-omics data (proteomics, metabolomics, transcriptomics etc.) directly from genotypes. To do this, we use extensive multi-omics data to train genetic scores using machine learning. Here, you can explore and download the genetic scores for a wide range of biomolecular traits in human blood as well as the summary statistics of their associations with key traits and diseases in the UK Biobank.

items.name: OntoCommons ontology catalogue
items.description: The purpose is to list the existing domain ontologies related to the OntoCommons project and use cases topics. On the Semantic Web, ontologies define the concepts and relationships used to describe a given domain and annotate data about it. In the OntoCommons Horizon CSA we are collecting ontologies about materials, construction, manufacturing and other industries. Here you can find the list of ontologies we have identified so far.

items.name: Open Archive for Miscellaneous Data
items.description: The Open Archive for Miscellaneous Data (OMIX) database is a data repository developed and maintained by the National Genomics Data Center (NGDC). The database specializes in descriptions of biological studies, including genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic, as well as data that do not fit in the structured archives at other databases in NGDC. It can accept various types of studies described via a simple format and enables researchers to upload supplementary information and link to it from the publication.

items.name: Open Calgary
items.description: Open Calgary is the City of Calgary Open Data Portal. In the spirit of openness, accountability and transparency, this portal facilitates data sharing, innovative ideas, and fostering a sense of collaboration among citizens.

items.name: Open Data Kingston
items.description: Open Data Kingston is the City of Kingston’s public open data portal that offers free access to a wide range of municipal datasets for anyone to explore, download, or use via APIs. It supports transparency, innovation, and public engagement by providing information on topics like demographics, transportation, environment, and city services. The portal also includes dashboards and tools to visualize data and help citizens, researchers, and developers derive insights.
licences: City of Kingston Open Data Licence 1.0

items.name: Open Energy Data Initiative
items.description: The Open Energy Data Initiative (OEDI) is a centralized repository of high-value energy research datasets aggregated from the U.S. Department of Energy’s Program Offices, National Laboratories and other collaborators.  It aggregates smaller, domain-specific repositories, allows direct data submissions, and supports big data in cloud-based data lakes.  Built to enable data discoverability, OEDI facilitates access to a broad network of findings, including the data available in technology-specific catalogs like the Geothermal Data Repository and Marine and Hydrokinetic Data Repository.

items.name: Open Government Data of Kerala
items.description: The Open Government Data of Kerala is the official open-data platform of the Government of Kerala that provides public access to datasets, documents, services, tools, and applications published by various state departments and agencies. It is designed to increase transparency in government operations and support innovation, research, and evidence-based decision-making by making data freely available in open formats. The portal enables users to search and discover data from many government sources in a single place, helping citizens, developers, and researchers to use and reuse information for diverse purposes.

items.name: Open Government Data Portal of Odisha
items.description: The Odisha Open Government Data Portal is the state of Odisha’s official platform for publishing open datasets collected by various government departments and organizations for public use. It is part of the Open Government Data initiative to increase transparency, accessibility, and innovation by making government data available in machine-readable formats to citizens, researchers, and developers. The portal allows users to discover, download, and reuse data across sectors such as health, education, environment, and more.

items.name: Open Government Data Portal of Sikkim
items.description: The Sikkim Open Government Data Portal is a public platform for discovering and downloading open datasets published by departments and agencies of the Government of Sikkim. It is part of India’s broader open data initiative and aims to increase transparency, accountability and reuse of government data by making it freely available in structured formats. The portal includes statistics, documents, tools and services across sectors that can be freely accessed, reused, and redistributed.

items.name: Open Hamilton
items.description: Open Hamilton is the City of Hamilton’s open data portal, providing public access to a variety of datasets covering city operations, infrastructure, demographics, environment, and more. It aims to promote transparency, civic engagement, and data-driven decision making by offering machine-readable data formats and tools for exploration.

items.name: Open Ottawa
items.description: Open Ottawa is the City of Ottawa’s official open data portal, offering free public access to a wide range of municipal datasets, maps, apps, and interactive tools. It’s designed to support transparency, civic engagement, and data-driven decision-making by letting anyone explore and download information about city services, infrastructure, environment, and more.

items.name: Open Penticton
items.description: Open Penticton is the City of Penticton’s open data hub, providing free public access to a wide range of municipal datasets including maps, infrastructure, environment, property, transportation, and more.

items.name: Open Reaction Database - Repository
items.description: The data repository for the Open Reaction Database (ORD). The ORD repository supports the sharing of structured reaction data. Their vision is that a consistent data representation and infrastructure to support data sharing will enable downstream applications that will greatly improve the state of the art with respect to computer-aided synthesis planning, reaction prediction, and other predictive chemistry tasks.

items.name: Open Research Data Online
items.description: Open Research Data Online (ORDO) is The Open University's research data repository. Based upon the Figshare platform, ORDO can be used for the storage of live research data, but is particularly useful for archiving and publishing research data supporting a publication or once a project is completed.

items.name: Open Researcher and Contributor ID Registry
items.description: ORCID is an open, non-profit, community-driven effort to create and maintain a registry of unique researcher identifiers and a transparent method of linking research activities and outputs to these identifiers. The ORCID Registry is a repository of unique researcher identifiers which allows researchers to manage a record of their research activities. In addition, there are APIs that support system-to-system communication and authentication. ORCID makes its code available under an open source license, and will post an annual public data file under a CC0 waiver for free download.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Open Universiteit research portal

items.name: Oxford University Research Archive
items.description:
The Oxford University Research Archive (ORA) is the institutional repository for the University of Oxford. ORA was established in 2007 as a permanent and secure online archive of research materials produced by members of the University and is managed by the Bodleian Libraries. ORA aims to provide access to the full text of as much of Oxford's academic research as possible, including articles, conference papers, theses, research data, working papers and posters. Digital object identifiers (DOIs) can be assigned to items in the repository for citation and attribution.

Making materials open access removes barriers that restrict access to research, allowing for free dissemination of full text content, available to anyone with Internet access. ORA promotes and encourages the sharing of the scholarly output produced by the members of the University that have been published under open access conditions, whilst additionally supporting University compliance with research funder policies and assessment. DataHub helps researchers address the full data life cycle for their institutional projects and provides a path to creating findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable (FAIR) data products. Policies and procedures governing laboratory data are critical to the integrity of our research. Equally important are the data management systems, which is why our researchers access the PACIFICA and DataHub systems that enable secure and quick access to research data. Our unique Living Laboratory is an information instrument enabling real-time, in situ studies of PNNL itself as a microcosm of the real world, securely providing researchers novel information about PNNL’s campus operations, thus facilitating research on complex systems. items.name: PANGAEA - Data Publisher for Earth and Environmental Science
items.description:
PANGAEA - Data Publisher for Earth & Environmental Sciences  has an almost 30-year history as an open-access library for archiving, publishing, and disseminating georeferenced data from the Earth, environmental, and biodiversity sciences. Originally evolving from a database for sediment cores, it is operated as a joint facility of the Alfred Wegener Institute, Helmholtz Centre for Polar and Marine Research (AWI) and the Center for Marine Environmental Sciences (MARUM) at the University of Bremen. PANGAEA holds a mandate from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO)  and is accredited as a World Radiation Monitoring Center (WRMC). It was further accredited as a World Data Center by the International Council for Science (ICS)  in 2001 and has been certified with the Core Trust Seal  since 2019. 
The successful cooperation between PANGAEA and the publishing industry along with the correspondent technical implementation enables the cross-referencing of scientific publications and datasets archived as supplements to these publications. PANGAEA is the recommended data repository of numerous international scientific journals.

items.name: Pergamos: NKUA's Unified Institutional Repository & Digital Library Platform
items.description:
Pergamos is the Unified Institutional Repository & Digital Library Platform of the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (NKUA). It has the ability to host any material, whether born digital or digitized, that is either owned and associated with our Institution or produced by the NKUA academic community.  The material hosted by Pergamos, is organised in collections, that, depending on its content, may have an administrator or curator from the staff of respective NKUA units that are related to the collection (who are responsible for the content of the collection they curate). This ensures that compliance with the relevant guidelines or regulations that may govern or affect the content is achieved.
In this respect, Pergamos comprises a large set of heterogeneous digital collections ranging from research and educational output (articles, papers, books, datasets, presentations, etc.) produced by the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens researchers, faculty and staff, to theses and dissertiations produced by NKUA's students, as well as extending to collections of archival, historical or cultural value. More specifically, Pergamos boasts of  more than 10 collections of diverse content, covering almost the entire thematic range of NKUA's Schools, while the total number of digital items reaches approximately 1,000,000 digital objects.
The description of the digital material is based on the Dublin Core metadata standard while the description of the archive material isbased upon the ISAD (G) standard. In each case and depending on the needs of the material, additions have been made to the description of the material either with the Dublin Core (DC qualified schema) specifications or with fields of local use and importance.
Pergamos implements the OAI-PMH (Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata Harvesting) metadata harvesting protocol, which makes its content searchable by various international websites, harvesters and search engines that support the OAI protocol, in excess of the more or less well known internet search engins (like Google, Bing, etc).
In addition, Pergamos' metadata are compatible with the Europeana Data Model (EDM) standard for platform interoperability with the Europeanana European Digital Library.
Moreover, Pergamos supports an open REST / JSON API for third-party hardware interoperability.
