items.description: ROHub is a holistic solution for the storage, lifecycle management and preservation of scientific investigations, campaigns and operational processes via research objects. It makes these resources available to others, allows to publish and release them through a DOI, and allows to discover and reuse pre-existing scientific knowledge. Built entirely around the research object concept and inspired by sustainable software management principles, ROHub is the reference platform implementing natively the full research object model and paradigm, including the latest RO-Crate specification, and which provides the backbone to a wealth of RO-centric applications and interfaces across different scientific communities. ROHub has been onboarded as a research enabling service in EOSC to support scientists in the adoption of FAIR and Open Science principles.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: RosDok
items.description: RosDok repository is the platform for online publication and long term archiving of digital documents for the University of Rostock.

items.name: RTU Research Outputs and Resources
items.description: ORTUS (Research Outputs and Resources) is Riga Technical University’s institutional research repository. It provides access to RTU scientific publications, research data, doctoral theses, patents, and university journals.

items.name: RUB Research Data Repository – Science Hub Plasma
items.description: The RUB Research Data Repository – Science Hub Plasma provides access to research data associated with scientific publications produced by its principal investigators. It focuses on low-temperature plasma physics and related fields, including plasma modelling, plasma chemistry, plasma medicine, and plasma-surface interactions. The repository uses a dedicated Plasma Metadata Schema to support the standardized documentation, findability, and reuse of research datasets in accordance with FAIR principles.
subjects: Atomic, Molecular, Optical and Plasma Physics

items.name: Rutgers University Community Repository
items.description: RUcore is the institutional digital repository of Rutgers University that collects, preserves, and provides access to the university’s scholarly and educational materials. It archives research outputs, theses and dissertations, faculty publications, datasets, and unique digital collections from the libraries’ special collections.

items.name: RWTH Publications
items.description: RWTH Publications is the institutional repository of RWTH Aachen University for preserving, documenting, and disseminating the university's scholarly output. It provides open access to publications as well as research datasets and software, while also serving as the official record of research produced by RWTH researchers. Covering all academic disciplines represented at the university, the repository supports long-term preservation, discoverability, and compliance with Open Access and research data management practices.

items.name: SABIO-RK Biochemical Reaction Kinetics Database
items.description: SABIO-RK is a database for biochemical reactions, their kinetic equations with their parameters, and the experimental conditions under which these parameters were measured.
licences: Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication & License (PDDL) v1.0

items.name: San José State University ScholarWorks
items.description: San José State University ScholarWorks collects, shares, and preserves the research, scholarship, and creative works of the SJSU community. They work with faculty, students, and staff to publish journals, curate faculty profiles, and showcase the intellectual output of the SJSU community to readers and scholars around the world.

items.name: Savannah
items.description: Savannah aims to be a central point for development, maintenance and distribution of official GNU software. In addition, for projects that support free software but are not part of GNU, a separate area of the resource is available. Savannah hosts free projects that run on free operating systems and without any proprietary software dependencies. The version Control systems available on Savannah are GNU Arch, GNU Bazaar, CVS, Git, Mercurial, and Subversion.
licences: GNU Affero General Public License (AGPL) v3.0 only

items.name: Scholars' Bank
items.description: Scholars' Bank is the open access repository for the intellectual work of faculty, students, and staff at the University of Oregon. It also houses materials from certain partner institution collections. Open access journals, student projects, theses and dissertations, pre- and post-print articles, instructional resources, and university archival material are all candidates for deposit.

items.name: ScholarSphere
items.description: ScholarSphere is an institutional repository managed by Penn State University Libraries. Anyone with a Penn State Access ID can deposit materials relating to the University’s teaching, learning, and research mission to ScholarSphere. All types of scholarly materials, including publications, instructional materials, creative works, and research data are accepted.

items.name: SciELO Data
items.description: SciELO Data is a multidisciplinary repository for deposition, preservation and dissemination of research data from articles submitted and approved for publication, already published in SciELO Network journals or deposited in SciELO Preprints.
licences: SciELO Terms and Conditions of Use

items.name: Science Data Bank
items.description: ScienceDB (Science Data Bank) is an open generalist data repository developed and maintained by the CNIC. It promotes the publication and reuse of scientific data. Researchers and journal publishers can use it to store, manage and share science data.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Scientific Data Repository
items.description: This project is the first to combine the notion of a data repository with real-time visual analytics for interactive data mining and exploratory analysis on the web. This large comprehensive collection of data is useful for making significant research findings as well as benchmark data sets for a wide variety of applications and domains and includes relational, attributed, heterogeneous, streaming, spatial, and time series data as well as non-relational machine learning data. All data sets are easily downloaded into a standard consistent format. We also have built a multi-level interactive visual analytics engine that allows users to visualize and interactively explore the data in a free-flowing manner.

items.name: Sciflection
items.description: Sciflection is a chemical database which allows researchers to publish and share their experiments as well as analytical data. Sciflection accepts structured data directly uploaded from Electronic Laboratory Notebooks (open enventory, Sciformation ELN, open for others) in JSON format. The repository is searchable by chemical structure, text parts, numeric parameters, etc.
domains: X-ray crystallography 3D molecular structure determination assay

items.name: SCIP (Substances of Concern In articles) Database
items.description: SCIP is the database for information on Substances of Concern In articles as such or in complex objects (Products) established under the Waste Framework Directive (2008/98/EC). Any company supplying articles containing SVHCs on the ECHA Candidate List in concentration above 0.1% w/w on EU market must submit information on these articles to the SCIP database from 5 January 2021.

items.name: Scopus
items.description: Scopus is an abstract and citation database of peer-reviewed literature across all research areas. It provides tools for visualization, tracking and analysis of its data.  Non-subscribed users access Scopus through Scopus Preview, which allows the searching of authors and source material (e.g. journal) titles.

items.name: searchRxiv
items.description: searchRxiv enables researchers to: post their searches, ensuring credit for all those involved; obtain a digital object identifier (DOI) for their search, enabling it to be cited; link searches to published articles as relevant; find it easier to follow best practice for structuring their search strategy; and easily find relevant searches in their subject area by searching across search strings as well as metadata describing those search strings.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: SEDICI
items.description: The Intellectual Creation Dissemination Service (SEDICI) is the Institutional Repository of the National University of La Plata, a free service created to house, preserve, and give visibility to the productions of the University's Academic Units.

items.name: SEGEMAR Repository
items.description: The SEGEMAR Institutional Repository is the open-access digital repository of the Argentine Geological and Mining Service (SEGEMAR). It provides access to geological, mining, environmental, hydrogeological, geophysical, and geoscientific information produced by SEGEMAR and related institutions in Argentina.

items.name: Sheffield Hallam University Research Data Archive
items.description: SHURDA (Sheffield Hallam University Research Data Archive) is the institutional repository for research datasets produced by researchers at Sheffield Hallam University. It preserves and provides access to both digital and non-digital research data, while also serving as a catalogue for datasets stored elsewhere. SHURDA promotes good research data management, long-term preservation, and data sharing by linking datasets to related research publications in the University's publication repository (SHURA).

items.name: Smithsonian Research Online
items.description: Smithsonian Research Online (SRO) is a digital service that collects, preserves, and distributes research data from the Smithsonian scholars. The Smithsonian Libraries collaborates with research and curatorial staff from the Smithsonian Institution’s 20 museums and 9 research centers to ensure the preservation of this legacy and to provide world-wide access to this intellectual output.

items.name: Software Heritage
items.description: The Software Heritage database stores source code with the goal of preserving software. Various metadata, including software origin and development history are retained. Software Heritage aims to ensure the availability, traceability and uniformity of the software it collects.

items.name: SourceForge
items.description: SourceForge is a free Open Source software repository providing services including version control, issue tracking and wiki pages.

items.name: Spectrum Research Repository
items.description: Spectrum, Concordia University's open-access research repository, preserves and centralizes access to the research created at Concordia.

items.name: Spiral
items.description: SPIRAL is the institutional open-access repository of Imperial College London that collects and provides online access to the college’s research outputs. It contains a wide variety of scholarly materials such as journal articles, conference papers, theses, reports, and datasets produced by Imperial researchers.

items.name: Standards for Reporting Enzymology Data Database
items.description: STRENDA DB is a storage and search platform supported by the Beilstein-Institut that incorporates the STRENDA Guidelines in a user-friendly, web-based system. If you are an author who is preparing a manuscript containing functional enzymology data, STRENDA DB provides you the means to ensure that your data sets are complete and valid before you submit them as part of a publication to a journal. Data entered in the STRENDA DB submission form are automatically checked for compliance with the STRENDA Guidelines; users receive warnings informing them when necessary information is missing. A successful formal compliance is confirmed by the awarding of a STRENDA Registry Number (SRN) and documented in a fact sheet (PDF) containing all input data that can be submitted with the manuscript to the journal. In addition, each dataset is assigned a DOI that allows reference and tracking of the data. The data become publicly available in the database only after the corresponding article has been peer-reviewed and published in a journal.

items.name: Statistics Canada
items.description: Statistics Canada (StatCan) is Canada’s national statistical agency and a public data platform. It provides official data and analysis about the country’s economy, society, population, and environment to support research, policy-making, and public information. The database includes results from censuses, surveys, and statistical programs, as well as data tables, microdata, and visualizations across many topics.

items.name: Stockholm University Figshare
items.description: Stockholm University Figshare is the institutional research data repository of Stockholm University. It enables researchers to preserve, publish, and share research datasets and other research outputs across all disciplines. The repository supports long-term preservation, assigns DOIs to published datasets, and promotes FAIR data management to improve the visibility and reuse of research outputs.

items.name: Stockholm University Library Dataverse
items.description: The Stockholm University Library Dataverse is a multidisciplinary research data repository managed by Stockholm University Library. It enables researchers to publish, preserve, and share research datasets in accordance with the FAIR principles, providing persistent DOIs and rich metadata to support discovery and citation. The repository promotes open science by making datasets reusable while also allowing access restrictions when required. It primarily serves researchers affiliated with Stockholm University, but its published datasets are openly accessible to the global research community.
licences: Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODC ODbL) v1.0

items.name: SUNScholarData
items.description: SUNScholarData is an institutional research data repository which can be used for the registration, archival storage, sharing and dissemination of research data produced or collected in relation to research conducted under the auspices of Stellenbosch University. The repository has a public interface which can be used for finding content. It also has private user accounts which can be used by Stellenbosch University users in order to upload, share or publish their research data. In addition to this Stellenbosch University researchers can also use SUNScholarData in order to collaborate with researchers from other institutions whilst working on their research projects. The repository creates a medium through which Stellenbosch University’s research data can be made findable and accessible. It also facilitates the interoperability and re-usability of the university’s research data.
licences: GNU Affero General Public License (AGPL) v3.0 only

items.name: Sustainable Digital Scholarship service
items.description: The Sustainable Digital Scholarship (SDS) service offers a platform for hosting and publishing digital research outputs as well as resources and consultations to support University of Oxford researchers to achieve digital sustainability. The SDS platform is a good fit for many non-traditional digital outputs and empowers researchers to manage and sustain innovative research projects, driving global visibility and championing open scholarship. On publication of a record, a versioned digital object identifier (DOI) is automatically assigned for citation and attribution.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: SWATHAtlas
items.description:
The SWATHAtlas at the Institute for Systems Biology is a resource for planning your DIA/SWATH™ experiments, depositing published experimental high-quality spectral assay libraries, and exploring the results of these uploaded datasets.
The SWATHAtlas project makes available spectral libraries that are designed to aid in SWATH™ data processing for several species. It enables the ability to query and explore a set of seed datasets on-line, custom analysis of SWATH™ datasets in the repository. Users have the option to analyze and repair spectral ion libraries using the DIALib-QC tool.

items.name: Tethys RDR
items.description: Tethys is an Open Access Research Data Repository of the GeoSphere Austria, which publishes and distributes georeferenced geoscientific research data generated at and in cooperation with the GeoSphere Austria. The research data publications and the associated metadata are predominantly provided in German or in English. The abstracts are provided in both languages. Tethys aims to provide published data sets as open data and in accordance with the FAIR Data Principles, findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable.

items.name: Texas Data Repository
items.description: The Texas Data Repository is a platform for publishing and managing datasets (and other data products) created by faculty, staff, and students at Texas higher education institutions. The repository is built in an open-source application called Dataverse, developed and used by Harvard University. The repository is hosted by the Texas Digital Library, a consortium of academic libraries in Texas with a proven history of providing shared technology services that support secure, reliable access to digital collections of research and scholarship. Researchers deposit data within the TDR to, for example, comply with funding requirements and ensure reliable, managed access for data.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: The Arabidopsis Information Resource
items.description: The Arabidopsis Information Resource (TAIR) maintains a database of genetic and molecular biology data for the model higher plant Arabidopsis thaliana. Data available from TAIR includes the complete genome sequence along with gene structure, gene product information, gene expression, DNA and seed stocks, genome maps, genetic and physical markers, publications, and information about the Arabidopsis research community. Gene product function data is updated every week from the latest published research literature and community data submissions.

items.name: The Data Platform for Plasma Technology
items.description: The interdisciplinary data platform INPTDAT provides easy access to research data and information from all fields of applied plasma physics and plasma medicine. It aims to support the findability, accessibility, interoperability and re-use of data for the low-temperature plasma physics community.
subjects: Atomic, Molecular, Optical and Plasma Physics
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: The Department of Energy Systems Biology Knowledgebase
items.description: KBase is a large-scale bioinformatics system that enables users to upload their own data, analyze it (along with collaborator and public data), build increasingly realistic models, and share and publish their workflows and conclusions. KBase aims to provide an integrated environment where knowledge and insights are created and multiplied.

items.name: The Environmental System Science Data Infrastructure for a Virtual Ecosystem
items.description: The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Environmental Systems Science Data Infrastructure for a Virtual Ecosystem (ESS-DIVE) is a data repository for Earth and environmental science data. ESS-DIVE is funded by the Data Management program within the Climate and Environmental Science Division under the DOE’s Office of Biological and Environmental Research program (BER), and is maintained by the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. ESS-DIVE archives and publicly shares data obtained from observational, experimental, and modeling research that is funded by the DOE’s Office of Science under its Subsurface Biogeochemical Research (SBR) and Terrestrial Ecosystem Science (TES) programs within the Environmental Systems Science (ESS) activity. The mission of ESS-DIVE is to preserve, expand access to, and improve usability of critical data generated through DOE-sponsored research of terrestrial and subsurface ecosystems in support of the DOE’s efforts to address some of society’s most pressing energy and environmental challenges.

items.name: The Hive: University of Utah Research Data Repository
items.description: The Hive is the University of Utah's research data repository provided by both the J. Willard Marriott Library and Eccles Health Sciences Library. It designed to broadly disseminate the intellectual contributions in research and creativity produced by the University's faculty, staff and students to ensure its longevity.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: The Materials Data Facility
items.description: MDF streamlines and automates data sharing, discovery, access and analysis by: 1) enabling data publication, regardless of data size, type, and location; 2) automating metadata extraction from submitted data into MDF metadata records (i.e., JSON formatted documents following the MDF schema) using open-source materials-aware extraction pipelines and ingest pipelines; and 3) unifying search across many materials data sources, including both MDF and other repositories with potentially different vocabularies and schemas. Currently, MDF stores 60 TB of data from simulation and experiment, and also indexes hundreds of datasets contained in external repositories, with millions of individual MDF metadata records created from these datasets to aid fine-grained discovery.

items.name: The Materials Project
items.description: The Materials Project (next-gen.materialsproject.org) is an open scientific database that provides computed data on known and predicted materials to support materials discovery. It contains information on hundreds of thousands of inorganic compounds, including crystal structures, electronic properties, and thermodynamic data generated through high-throughput simulations.

items.name: The National Energy Research Scientific Computing Center
items.description: The National Energy Research Scientific Computing Center (NERSC) is a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Science User Facility that serves as the primary high-performance computing center for scientific research sponsored by the Office of Science. Located at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, the NERSC Center serves more than 7,000 scientists at national laboratories and universities researching a wide range of problems in combustion, climate modeling, fusion energy, materials science, physics, chemistry, computational biology, and other disciplines.
licences: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory Web Policy Terms & Conditions

items.name: The Open Science Framework
items.description: The Open Science Framework (OSF) is a free and open free, open repository and platform to enable collaboration and support the entire research lifecycle: planning, execution, reporting, archiving, and discovery. Features include automated versioning, logging of all actions, collaboration support, free and unlimited file storage, registrations, and connections to other tools/services (ie. Dropbox, figshare, Amazon S3, Dataverse, GitHub). It is 100% free to researchers, open source, and intended for use in all domain areas. OSF has an open, public API to support broad indexing, as well as a partnership with Internet Archive for long-term preservation with a $250k preservation fund and an IMLS grant for transfer to Internet Archive (currently in progress). The OSF supports embargoing during peer review via a view-only link with the ability to anonymize contributor list. It also provides managed access by allowing access requests and private sharing settings. OSF is a non-profit with direct funder support through grants, government contracts, and community memberships.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: The pan-African Open Access Platform
items.description: AfricArXiv is a free community-led digital archive for African research that provides a platform for African scientists to upload their working papers, preprints, accepted manuscripts (post-prints), and published papers. AfricArXiv aims for the dissemination of African scholarly content: 1) to a global audience, and 2) allows for knowledge exchange between African scholars and non-African researchers of African studies and other disciplines by providing options to link data and code along with article versioning. AfricArxiv provides African scientists from all disciplines to share their research outputs, including preprints, postprints, code and data free of cost.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: The Perovskite Database Project
items.description: The Perovskite Database Project is an open-access repository that collects and organizes experimental data on perovskite devices, especially solar cells. It aggregates data extracted from thousands of scientific publications and allows users to explore, search, filter, and visualize the dataset with interactive tools.

items.name: The Radboud Data Repository
items.description: The Radboud Data Repository (RDR) is an institutional repository that supports Radboud University and Radboudumc (Nijmegen, the Netherlands) researchers in archiving and sharing collected, processed, or analyzed data. The repository allows safe long-term (at least 10 years) storage of large datasets. The RDR promotes findability of datasets by providing a DOI and rich metadata fields and allows researchers to easily manage data access.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication
Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-BY) v1.0
Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODC ODbL) v1.0
Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication & License (PDDL) v1.0

items.name: ThermoML Archive
items.description: The ThermoML Archive is a storage facility of experimental thermophysical and thermochemical property data. The repository was created through the cooperation between the Thermodynamics Research Center (TRC), NIST and: Journal of Chemical and Engineering Data (JCED), Journal of Chemical Thermodynamics, Fluid Phase Equilibria, Thermochimica Acta, and the International Journal of Thermophysics. The ThermoML files corresponding to articles in the journals are available with permission of the journal publishers.

items.name: TU Graz Repository
items.description: The TU Graz Repository is the institutional repository of Graz University of Technology (Austria). It enables researchers to preserve, publish, and share research outputs, including datasets, software, publications, and open educational resources.

items.name: TU Wien Research Data
items.description: TU Wien Research Data is an institutional repository of TU Wien to enable storing, sharing and publishing of digital objects, in particular research data. It facilitates the funders' requirements for open access to research data and the FAIR principles by making research output findable, accessible, interoperable and re-usable. This service is developed by the TU Wien Center for Research Data Management and hosted by Campus IT. The repository has been certified with Core Trust Seal in September 2025.

items.name: U.S. Antarctic Program Data Center
items.description: The U.S. Antarctic Program Data Center (USAP-DC) provides a central USAP Project Catalog for all projects funded by the NSF Antarctic program and a Data Repository for research datasets derived from these projects. Data managed include the NSF research related glaciology data collection formerly managed through NSIDC. Datasets are registered in the Antarctic Master Directory to comply with the Antarctic Treaty and represent the U.S. in Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research (SCAR) activities.
licences: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 United States (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 US)

items.name: UA Campus Repository
items.description: The UA Campus Repository is a publicly available institutional repository. Sharing UA research with the world, the UA Campus Repository supports the widest possible dissemination of UA research and scholarship. Through partnerships with campus contributors, the repository facilitates access to the research, publications, creative works and teaching materials of the University by collecting, sharing and archiving content selected and deposited by faculty, researchers, staff and affiliated contributors. The repository also provides access to digital collections developed by the University of Arizona Libraries and Special Collections.

items.name: UAL Research Online
items.description: UAL Research Online is the online showcase of the research produced at University of the Arts London.
licences: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs 2.0 UK: England & Wales (CC BY-NC-ND 2.0 UK)

items.name: UBC Dataverse Collection
items.description: The UBC Dataverse Collection is a research data repository within Borealis that provides access to datasets produced by researchers at the University of British Columbia. It contains research data from a wide range of disciplines, including health sciences, environmental sciences, agriculture, and other fields. The datasets can be accessed, downloaded, and cited through persistent identifiers such as DOIs.

items.name: Ubiquity Press Dataverse
items.description: The Ubiquity Press Dataverse supports the publication and long-term preservation of research datasets associated with Ubiquity Press publications. It enables researchers to openly share data, software, and other research outputs, making them citable through persistent identifiers and easily discoverable. The repository promotes transparency, reproducibility, and open science by providing free access to datasets linked to scholarly articles and books.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: UC Irvine Machine Learning Repository
items.description: The UCI Machine Learning Repository is a collection of databases, domain theories, and data generators that are used by the machine learning community for the empirical analysis of machine learning algorithms.

items.name: UC San Diego Library Digital Collections
items.description: The UC San Diego Library Digital Collections (DC) is a curated repository for sharing and preserving research data. Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs) are provided for all research datasets, so the data can be cited easily and accessed persistently. The contents of the DC are replicated in Chronopolis, a certified, geographically distributed preservation system designed to prevent catastrophic loss of data. Most research datasets are openly accessible, although submissions are restricted to University affiliates.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: UCL Research Data Repository
items.description: The UCL Research Data Repository is an institutional platform provided by University College London for archiving, publishing, and preserving research data and associated outputs created by UCL staff and postgraduate researchers.

items.name: UCLA Dataverse
items.description:
The UCLA Library adopted Dataverse, an open source web application designed for sharing, preserving, and using research data. UCLA Dataverse will enable people in publishing and tracking research data, text software, scripts, and data visualizations created from research projects at UCLA. The data can be made publicly available, discoverable, linkable, and ultimately, reusable. The Data Science center will support the ability of research groups, centers, schools, and departments to obtain their own sub-dataverse that they can administer with guidance and training.
UCLA Dataverse will allow data, text, software, scripts, data visualizations, etc., created from research projects at UCLA to be made publicly available, widely discoverable, linkable, and ultimately, reusable. We will also support the ability of research groups, centers, schools and departments to obtain their own sub-dataverse that they can administer with guidance and training from the Data Science Center.

items.name: UdG Digital Repository
items.description: DUGiDocs is the institutional repository of the Universitat de Girona. Its aim is to preserve, spread and make visible the intellectual production issued from research and teaching lead at the UdG, such as degree final reports, master reports and doctorate research reports by university students as well as articles in scientific periodicals.

items.name: UEL Research Repository
items.description: The UEL Research Repository preserves and disseminates open access publications, research data, and theses created by members of the University of East London.

items.name: Ulster University Research Portal
items.description: Ulster University Research Portal is Ulster University’s digital repository of research material created by Ulster University’s researchers. The online portal showcases the research and scholarly output of the university across all subjects and disciplines. The primary aim of UU Research Portal is to increase the impact of the university's research, share knowledge and provide a mechanism for Open Access.

items.name: UNB Libraries Dataverse Research Data Repository
items.description: The UNB Dataverse Repository is an institutional research data repository operated by the University of New Brunswick. It enables researchers to deposit, preserve, share, discover, and cite research datasets from any discipline using the open-source Dataverse platform. Each dataset is accompanied by rich metadata, documentation, and persistent identifiers to support long-term preservation and data reuse in accordance with FAIR principles.

items.name: UNC Dataverse
items.description: UNC Dataverse is a research data repository hosted by the Research Data Management Core at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (UNC). UNC Dataverse is an open access repository that accepts data deposits from UNC-affiliated researchers, research groups, institutions, journals, and other entities from all disciplinary domains.  UNC Dataverse offers value-added features that support archiving, discovery, and sharing of research data that align with FAIR principles for findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable data.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: UNESCO Digital Library
items.description: The UNESCO Digital Library provides access to publications, documents and other materials either produced by UNESCO or pertaining to UNESCO’s fields of competence. It is constantly enriched with new publications and documents produced by UNESCO, as well as with acquisitions, resources shared by other institutions and donations. The UNESCO Digital Library is the repository of UNESCO’s institutional memory and a source of information on UNESCO activities (in education, natural sciences, social and human sciences, culture, and communication and information), with more than 350,000 documents dating back to 1945.

items.name: University Digital Conservancy
items.description: The University Digital Conservancy (UDC) is a program of the University of Minnesota Libraries that encompasses the institutional repository, the data repository, and web archiving for the University of Minnesota.

items.name: University of Alberta Borealis-Dataverse
items.description: University of Alberta Borealis-Dataverse is a research data repository service for supporting the deposit and open discovery of research data, and is freely available for use by members of the University of Alberta community.

items.name: University of Arizona Research Data Repository
items.description: ReDATA is the University of Arizona's data repository. Most datasets are publicly available however new submissions are open to university affiliates only.
licences: University of Arizona Terms and Conditions

items.name: University of Auckland Figshare Repository
items.description: The University of Auckland Figshare repository is an institutional research data platform where researchers at the University of Auckland can store, share, and publish their research outputs, such as datasets, figures, and other research materials.

items.name: University of Bath Research Data Archive
items.description: The University of Bath Research Data Archive is the institutional repository for research data produced by researchers at the University of Bath. It preserves, manages, and shares datasets that support published research, making them discoverable through standardized metadata and persistent identifiers (DOIs). The repository promotes long-term preservation, research transparency, and data reuse while supporting both open and controlled access where appropriate.
licences: CERN Open Hardware Licence Version 2 - Permissive
CERN Open Hardware Licence Version 2 - Strongly Reciprocal
CERN Open Hardware Licence Version 2 - Weakly Reciprocal
Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: University of Birmingham eData Repository
items.description: The UBIRA eData repository is an institutional research data archive run by the University of Birmingham for registering, preserving, and publishing research datasets produced by its researchers. It supports a wide range of disciplines, including natural sciences, engineering, social sciences, and the humanities.

items.name: University of Guelph Research Data Repositories
items.description: The University of Guelph Research Data Repositories provide long-term stewardship of research datasets created at or in cooperation with the University of Guelph.

items.name: University of Hong Kong DataHub
items.description: The University of Hong Kong (HKU) DataHub is a comprehensive repository for research data and other forms of scholarly outputs provided by the University of Hong Kong Libraries. DataHub, powered by Figshare, is the cloud platform for storing, citing, sharing, and discovering research data and all scholarly outputs. It collects, preserves, and provides stable, long-term global open access to a wide range of research data and scholarly outputs created by HKU researchers and postgraduate students.

items.name: University of Melbourne Figshare Archive
items.description: The University of Melbourne Figshare is an institutional archive that stores the research output from the University of Melbourne.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: University of Nebraska-Lincoln Data Repository
items.description: The University of Nebraska-Lincoln Data Repository (UNLDR) is a data repository built in support of researchers at UNL. Hosted and curated by UNL Libraries, UNLDR is committed to preservation of and continued access to dataset resultant from research conducted at UNL.

items.name: University of Pretoria Research Data Repository
items.description: UP Research Data Repository is the institutional data repository of University of Pretoria. It runs on a Figshare platform and is designed to publish, preserve, and share research datasets from UP.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: University of Reading Research Data Archive
items.description: The University of Reading Research Data Archive is a multidisciplinary online service for the registration, preservation and publication of research data produced or collected at the University of Reading.

items.name: University of Salford Data Repository
items.description: The University of Salford Figshare platform is the University of Salford’s institutional research data repository where researchers can archive, publish, and share their research datasets and other outputs. It provides a secure and searchable space for storing data in a wide range of formats, supports metadata and versioning.

items.name: University of Sheffield - Open Research Data
items.description: ORDA is the University of Sheffield’s research data repository, which enables University research data to be shared, discovered, and preserved. It is provided by Figshare, and managed and curated by the University Library’s Research Data Management team. Researchers are strongly encouraged to deposit their data in ORDA, unless there is a subject-specific repository or data centre which is commonly used in their field. Each record placed in ORDA is also provided with a Datacite DOI. ORDA is ideal for non-sensitive data that can be made publicly available online. While depositors can restrict or embargo access to data in ORDA if required,  there may be more appropriate long-term storage options for sensitive data in other repositories with varying levels of controlled access, or in University networked storage.

items.name: University of Surrey Open Research repository
items.description: The University of Surrey Open Research Repository is the institutional repository for preserving and sharing the university’s research outputs, including datasets, publications, theses, and other scholarly materials. It supports open research by making research outputs discoverable, accessible, and reusable in line with the FAIR principles.

items.name: University of Tasmania Research Data Portal
items.description: The University of Tasmania Research Data Portal (RDP) enables UTAS researchers to securely store and publish their datasets. Datasets published in RDP are publicly available through the Research Data Australia Search Portal (https://researchdata.edu.au/).
licences: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Australia (CC BY 3.0 AU)

items.name: University of Victoria Dataverse
items.description: The University of Victoria Dataverse Collection of research data repositories serves our faculty, researchers, and students. Dataverse is a general purpose repository, suitable for all disciplines, and accepts a wide range of data types and formats. All deposited files are held in a secure environment on Canadian servers, and depositors can choose to make content available publicly, to specific individuals, or to keep it locked.

items.name: University of Virginia Dataverse: LibraData
items.description: LibraData is a place for researchers from the University of Virginia (UVA) to share data and other products of research publicly. It is UVA's local instance of the Dataverse software. LibraData is part of the Libra Scholarly Repository suite of services which includes works of UVA scholarship such as articles, books, theses, and data.

items.name: University of Warsaw Research Data Repository
items.description: University of Warsaw Research Data Repository aims to collect, archive, preserve and make available all types of research data. Storing and making data available is possible for users affiliated with the University of Warsaw, Poland, or those involved in projects carried out in partnership with the University of Warsaw. Browsing and downloading publicly available research data is open to all interested.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: UNM Digital Repository
items.description: UNM’s Digital Repository is an open access institutional repository created to preserve, gather and disseminate scholarship, research and cultural works created by UNM faculty, staff and students within UNM departments, centers and programs. The repository supports teaching and lifelong learning within the UNM campus and broader New Mexico community by making deposited materials permanently and freely accessible.

items.name: UNSWorks
items.description: The UNSWorks (UNSW Open Access Institutional Repository) is the institutional repository of UNSW Sydney (University of New South Wales, Australia), designed to collect, preserve, and disseminate the university’s research outputs. It provides access to a wide range of scholarly materials, including publications, theses, and research datasets, supporting open access and long-term preservation of research outputs. The repository enables UNSW researchers to make their work discoverable and accessible worldwide.

items.name: UPF Digital Repository
items.description: The UPF Digital Repository is the institutional repository of Pompeu Fabra University (Barcelona), designed to collect and disseminate the university’s research output. It includes a wide range of academic materials such as journal articles, working papers, theses, dissertations, and research reports. It also hosts research datasets and supplementary materials supporting publications. The repository is multidisciplinary, covering research produced across all academic fields at the university.

items.name: UQ eSpace
items.description:
The University of Queensland's institutional repository, UQ eSpace, aims to create global visibility and accessibility of UQ’s scholarly research by:

Enhancing discovery of UQ research via search engines such as Google and Trove
Allowing researchers to deposit scholarly works, datasets and open access materials and to view associated metrics
Maintaining a complete and accurate collection of all UQ scholarly works and data sets that feeds into central UQ systems including UQ Researchers and the Academic Portal
Enabling government reporting such as Australian Research Council’s Excellence in Research for Australia and the Engagement and Impact Assessment
Supporting the deposit of open access works to make UQ research globally accessible
Preserving and making digitised materials accessible to the world including HDR theses, photographs, audio materials, videos, manuscripts and other original works.

items.name: USU Institutional Repository
items.description: The Universitas Sumatera Utara (USU) Repository is the institutional repository of the University of Sumatera Utara (Indonesia), designed to collect, preserve, and disseminate the university’s scholarly outputs. It provides access to academic works such as theses, dissertations, scientific publications, research reports, and other digital documents produced by the university community.

items.name: UVaDOC
items.description: UVaDOC is the institutional digital repository of the University of Valladolid that provides open access to a wide range of academic, scientific, teaching, and institutional documents produced by the university community. It includes full-text resources such as research articles, theses, datasets, educational materials, and historical collections, all freely accessible online.

items.name: UWA Profiles and Research Repository
items.description: The UWA Profiles and Research Repository is an open platform where you can discover University of Western Australia (UWA) staff, find information about their research, teaching, grants, and activities, and access their research outputs.
licences: UWA Profiles and Research Repository Copyright and Take-down Requests

items.name: UWE Bristol Research Data Repository
items.description: The UWE Bristol Research Repository is an open access online repository providing a central record of the University's research output as well as, whenever possible, immediate access to the full text. It covers the whole range of UWE Bristol's output including books, book chapters, conference papers, images, and journal articles.

items.name: UWinnipeg Borealis
items.description: The UWinnipeg Borealis is the University of Winnipeg’s research data repository hosted on the Canadian Borealis Dataverse platform. It stores and shares finalized research datasets created by University of Winnipeg researchers, making them discoverable and citable online.

items.name: VinaR - Repository of the Vinča Institute of Nuclear Sciences
items.description:
VinaR, i.e. Vinča Repository, is a joint digital repository of the all laboratories and departments in Vinča Institute of Nuclear Sciences, University of Belgrade. VinaR provides open access to the publications, as well as to other outputs of the research projects implemented in these institutions.
The software platform (DSpace) meets the current requirements that apply to the dissemination of scholarly publications and it is compatible with relevant international infrastructures.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Virginia Tech Data Repository
items.description: The purpose of the Virginia Tech Data Repository is to highlight, preserve, and provide access to research products (e.g. datasets) of the Virginia Tech community, and in doing so help to disseminate the intellectual output of the university in its land-grant mission. The Virginia Tech Data Repository and Virginia Tech serve the Commonwealth of Virginia, the nation, and the world’s community through the discovery and dissemination of new knowledge.

items.name: WALTZ-DB 2.0
items.description: WALTZ-DB 2.0 is a database for characterizing short peptides for their amyloid fiber-forming capacities. The majority of the data comes from electron microscopy, FTIR and Thioflavin-T experiments done by the Switch lab. Apart from that class of data we also provide the amyloid annotation for several other short peptides found in current scientific research papers. Structural models of the potential amyloid cores are provided for every peptide entry.

items.name: WashU Research Data
items.description: WashU Research Data (Washington University Research Data repository) is a research data repository that allows researchers to share and access datasets across a wide range of disciplines. It contains various types of research data, including textual, tabular, geospatial, imagery, code, and 3D data. The repository supports the long-term preservation, discovery, and reuse of research data.

items.name: White Rock Open Data Portal
items.description: The City of White Rock Open Data portal offers over 150 structured datasets covering many aspects of city administration and public services. Data types include water treatment results (metals, microbiological indicators), building permits, business licences, city service requests (e.g. streetlight repairs, graffiti removal), and voting records of city council meetings.

items.name: Wikidata
items.description: Wikidata is a free and open knowledge base that can be read and edited by both humans and machines. Wikidata acts as central storage for the structured data of its Wikimedia sister projects including Wikipedia, Wikivoyage, Wiktionary, Wikisource, and others. Wikidata also provides support to many other sites and services beyond just Wikimedia projects. The content of Wikidata is available under a free license, exported using standard formats, and can be interlinked to other open data sets on the linked data web.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: Wolfram Data Repository
items.description: The Wolfram Data Repository is a public resource that hosts an expanding collection of computable datasets, curated and structured to be suitable for immediate use in computation, visualization, analysis and more. Building on the Wolfram Data Framework and the Wolfram Language, the Wolfram Data Repository provides a uniform system for storing data and making it immediately computable and useful. With datasets of many types and from many sources, the Wolfram Data Repository is built to be a global resource for public data and data-backed publication.

items.name: Wolverhampton Intellectual Repository and E-Theses
items.description: Wolverhampton Intellectual Repository and E-Theses (WIRE) is the University of Wolverhampton's open access collection of research outputs produced within the institution, by students, academic or professional staff. All content is openly available, other than valid exemptions for selected embargoed records. Any type of research output authored by a member of the University of Wolverhampton’s research community can be submitted to WIRE, from journal articles, conference contributions and book chapters to exhibitions and digital or visual media.

items.name: WorkflowHub
items.description: The WorkflowHub is a registry of scientific workflows.  WorkflowHub aims to facilitate discovery and re-use of workflows in an accessible and interoperable way. This is achieved through extensive use of open standards and tools, including CWL, RO-Crate, Bioschemas and GA4GH's TRS API, in accordance with the FAIR principles. WorkflowHub supports workflows of any type in its native repository.

items.name: World Ocean Atlas
items.description: The World Ocean Atlas (WOA) is a collection of objectively analyzed, quality controlled temperature, salinity, oxygen, phosphate, silicate, and nitrate means based on profile data from the World Ocean Database (WOD). It can be used to create boundary and/or initial conditions for a variety of ocean models, verify numerical simulations of the ocean, and corroborate satellite data.

items.name: WueData
items.description: WueData is the institutional research data repository of the Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg (JMU). It enables the publication of research data. The focus of the cross-disciplinary repository is on research data from subjects that do not yet have their own discipline-specific infrastructures for research data management.

items.name: WURM
items.description: The WURM project is a scientific database providing computed physical properties of minerals, including crystal structures, dielectric parameters, and Raman and infrared spectra for a wide range of minerals. These properties are calculated using quantum mechanical methods such as density‑functional theory and presented in an accessible online format.

items.name: WUT Base of Knowledge
items.description: The WUT Base of Knowledge is the Warsaw University of Technology’s institutional research repository. It collects, preserves, and provides access to research outputs, scientific publications, and associated digital materials from the university community.

items.name: Wyoming Data Repository
items.description: The Wyoming Data Repository (WDR) supports open discovery and preservation of data outputs produced by University of Wyoming and Wyoming Community College researchers.

items.name: Yabelana
items.description: Yabelana is the institutional research data repository of the University of KwaZulu-Natal (UKZN), South Africa. It enables UKZN researchers to preserve, manage, publish, and share a wide range of research data, including datasets, software, images, videos, and other research outputs. The repository supports long-term preservation, assigns DOIs to datasets, and promotes the FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles to improve the visibility and reuse of research data.

items.name: Yareta
items.description: Yareta is the University of Geneva’s digital research data repository designed to archive, preserve, and share research data over the long term.

items.name: Zenodo
items.description: Zenodo is a generalist research data repository built and developed by OpenAIRE and CERN. It was developed to aid Open Science and is built on open source code. Zenodo helps researchers receive credit by making the research results citable and through OpenAIRE integrates them into existing reporting lines to funding agencies like the European Commission. Citation information is also passed to DataCite and onto the scholarly aggregators. Content is available publicly under any one of 400 open licences (from opendefinition.org and spdx.org). Restricted and Closed content is also supported. Free for researchers below 50 GB/dataset. Content is both online on disk and offline on tape as part of a long-term preservation policy. Zenodo supports managed access (with an access request workflow) as well as embargoing generally and during peer review. The base infrastructure of Zenodo is provided by CERN, a non-profit IGO. Projects are funded through grants.
licences: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication

items.name: ZivaHub
items.description: ZivaHub is the institutional open data repository of the University of Cape Town (UCT). It serves as a platform for publishing, preserving, and sharing research data and scholarly outputs produced by UCT students and staff.
